docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Terms used throughout this documentation, in alphabetical order. Abbreviations are expanded the first time they appear on each page.

Access policy The policy of a contract definition that decides whether a consumer sees an offer in the catalog. Evaluated on every catalog request. See Catena-X policies. Asset The provider's description of something it offers, usually a backend API. It holds public properties (shown in the catalog), privateProperties and a dataAddress that tells the data plane how to reach the backend. BDRS BPN-DID Resolution Service. A Catena-X dataspace service that maps business partner numbers (BPNs) to DIDs and back. BPN, BPNL Business Partner Number. The Catena-X identifier of a legal entity (BPNL…), site (BPNS…) or address (BPNA…). Connectors identify participants by BPNL or by DID. Business partner group A named group of BPNs that a provider maintains in its connector and uses in access or contract policies through the BusinessPartnerGroup constraint. Catalog The list of datasets and contract offers a provider shows to a specific consumer. Filtered by access policies. Consumer The participant that requests data. The same connector can act as consumer and provider. Contract agreement The signed result of a successful negotiation: which asset, which policy, between which participants. Required to start a transfer. Contract definition The provider-side link between a set of assets (selected by an assetsSelector), one access policy and one contract policy. Creates the offers in the catalog. Contract negotiation The state machine in which consumer and provider agree on an offer. Ends in FINALIZED (agreement) or TERMINATED. Contract policy (usage policy) The policy of a contract definition that is checked during negotiation and becomes part of the agreement. Control plane The runtime that manages catalog, negotiations, agreements and transfer processes, and exposes the Management API and the Dataspace Protocol endpoints. Credential service (wallet) The component that stores a participant's verifiable credentials and issues verifiable presentations on request. Data address A typed description of where data lives (for example HttpData with a baseUrl). Assets have one, and the EDR is one too. Data plane The runtime that moves data once a transfer is started. For HTTP pull it exposes a public endpoint that consumers call with the token from the EDR. Data plane signaling (DPS) The upstream EDC protocol between control plane and data plane to start, suspend and terminate data flows. DCP Decentralized Claims Protocol: how connectors request and verify verifiable presentations from each other's credential services. DID Decentralized Identifier, for example did:web:example.com:bpnl000000000001. Resolves to a DID document with keys and service endpoints. DSP Dataspace Protocol: the protocol control planes use with each other for catalog, negotiation and transfer. EDR Endpoint Data Reference. A data address with an endpoint and a short-lived access token that the provider sends to the consumer when a pull transfer starts. Tractus-X EDC caches EDRs and can refresh their tokens. See EDRs and token refresh. Extension A Java module that plugs into an EDC runtime through the ServiceExtension interface. Tractus-X EDC is a set of extensions on top of upstream EDC. See Writing extensions. JSON-LD JSON for Linked Data. All Management API and DSP payloads are JSON-LD; terms are expanded to IRIs using the @context. See JSON-LD and namespaces. Management API The authenticated HTTP API of the control plane through which your own applications manage assets, policies, negotiations, transfers and EDRs. ODRL Open Digital Rights Language, the W3C policy language EDC policies are written in. Participant A company in the dataspace, identified by a DID (and in Catena-X by a BPNL). Provider The participant that offers data. STS Secure Token Service. Issues the self-issued identity tokens a connector attaches to DSP requests in DCP. Transfer process The state machine that starts, suspends and terminates the data flow for an agreement. Types include HTTP pull and provider push. Verifiable credential (VC) / verifiable presentation (VP) A signed statement about a participant (for example "is a Catena-X member"), and a signed bundle of credentials presented to a verifier.

docs.title: What is Tractus-X EDC?
docs.text:
Tractus-X EDC is a dataspace connector: a piece of software every company runs to take part in a dataspace such as Catena-X, Factory-X, Construct-X or any other dataspace that speaks the Dataspace Protocol (DSP) and uses the Decentralized Claims Protocol (DCP) for authorization. It lets a company offer data to partners under conditions it defines, and obtain data from partners under conditions they define, without uploading anything to a central platform.

It is the Eclipse Tractus-X distribution of the Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC) connector. EDC is a framework; Tractus-X EDC turns it into ready-to-run Docker images and Helm charts, and adds what dataspaces need: verifiable credential checks, EDR caching with token refresh, connector discovery and more. Dataspace-specific rules, such as the Catena-X policies and the Business Partner Number (BPN) identity, are added as extensions. See Supported dataspaces.

docs.title: The problem it solves
docs.text:
Two companies want to share data, for example a supplier's quality data with a car maker. Both need answers to the same questions before a single byte moves:

  • Who are you? The provider must be sure who is asking, without a shared user database.
  • Are you allowed? Only partners who hold the right credentials (in Catena-X, for example, membership and a signed framework agreement) or who belong to a given business partner group may see an offer.
  • Under which terms? Usage purpose, duration and other conditions must be agreed and recorded.
  • How do I get the data? Once agreed, the consumer needs a secure, short-lived way to call the provider's backend.

A connector answers all four, in a standard way, so every participant can talk to every other participant.

docs.title: The four ideas you need
docs.text:
• Catalog and offers

    A provider registers assets (pointers to its backend APIs), attaches policies, and publishes them as contract offers in its catalog. Consumers browse the catalog.

  • Contract negotiation

    The consumer requests an offer. The provider checks the consumer's credentials against the policy and, if all is fine, both sides store the same contract agreement.

  • Transfer and EDR

    With an agreement the consumer starts a transfer process. For pull transfers it receives an Endpoint Data Reference (EDR): an endpoint plus a short-lived token for the provider's data plane.

  • Decentralised identity

    Nobody logs in. Each connector proves who it is with verifiable credentials held in its own wallet, using the Decentralized Claims Protocol (DCP) and Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs).

docs.title: Two planes
docs.text:
A Tractus-X EDC deployment has two runtimes:

Control plane Data plane Job Decides whether data may flow Moves the data Talks to Other control planes (Dataspace Protocol), your apps (Management API), wallets Your backend systems, consumers holding an EDR Stores Assets, policies, contract definitions, negotiations, agreements, transfer processes, EDRs Data flows and token state Scales with Number of negotiations and transfers Data volume

Keeping them separate means the data path can scale and be placed close to the data, while the negotiation logic stays in one well-protected place. See Architecture for the full picture.

docs.title: What Tractus-X adds on top of EDC
docs.text:
• Catena-X policies (for the Catena-X dataspace): the constraints of standard CX-0152 (Membership, FrameworkAgreement, UsagePurpose, BusinessPartnerNumber, BusinessPartnerGroup, …) with validation on creation. Read more
  • BPN identity (Catena-X): business partner numbers resolved to DIDs through the BPN-DID Resolution Service (BDRS), and business partner groups for access control.
  • EDR management: one call to negotiate and start a transfer, an EDR cache, and token refresh so consumers keep access without renegotiating. Read more
  • Connector discovery: find a partner's connector and supported protocol versions from its DID document.
  • Operations: PostgreSQL schema migrations, HashiCorp Vault integration, Helm charts, and backward compatibility for older Dataspace Protocol versions.

The extension catalogue lists every Tractus-X module.

docs.title: What Tractus-X EDC is not
docs.text:
• Not a wallet. Credentials are held by a credential service (wallet) that you operate or rent. The connector asks it for verifiable presentations.
  • Not a business application. The connector exposes APIs; a business application (or a tool such as the Tractus-X SDK) drives them.
  • Not a data store. Data stays in your backend; the data plane proxies or pushes it on request.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Want to try it? Start with the local quick start and Tutorial 1.
  • Want the details? Read the architecture overview.
  • Unsure about a term? See the glossary.

docs.title: Why Tractus-X EDC?
docs.text:
Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC) is a framework: a set of modules and extension points from which you assemble your own connector. It implements the Dataspace Protocol (DSP) and the Decentralized Claims Protocol (DCP), but it leaves the runtime, the packaging, the dataspace rules and the operations to you.

Tractus-X EDC is that connector, ready to run. It is built on a pinned EDC version and adds the extensions, the release artefacts, the tests and the community that a company needs to join a dataspace and to stay in it across releases: Catena-X out of the box, and Manufacturing-X dataspaces such as Factory-X and Construct-X, or any other dataspace that speaks the Dataspace Protocol (DSP) and uses the Decentralized Claims Protocol (DCP) for authorization, through dataspace extensions.

  • Ready to run

    Released control plane, data plane and in-memory runtimes, as OSS images on Docker Hub: multi-architecture, non-root, for every release.

    Docker Sponsored OSS

  • Helm charts

    The tractusx-connector chart (production, with optional PostgreSQL and Vault) and tractusx-connector-memory (testing), published to the Tractus-X Helm repository and tested on every CI run.

    Deploy in five minutes

  • Catena-X rules built in

    The Catena-X policy constraints (CX-0152), Business Partner Number and BPN group checks, the BPN-DID Resolution Service (BDRS) client and the Catena-X credential scopes.

    Catena-X policies

  • Extensible for your dataspace

    A dataspace-agnostic core: the rules of Factory-X, Construct-X or your own dataspace are added as extensions, the way the Catena-X rules are.

    Supported dataspaces

  • Any DCP wallet

    Works with the open-source Tractus-X Identity Hub, SAP's managed DIV, or any wallet that implements DCP.

    Wallets you can use

  • Production-ready

    Released for production and running in production in Catena-X. As with any open-source software, you run it at your own risk (Apache License 2.0, no warranty).

    Production checklist

  • A mature release cycle, an open roadmap

    A release every quarter, aligned with Eclipse Tractus-X: release candidates tested before the final release, and bugfix releases that contain only the fix. The roadmap is planned in public, so any company can see what comes next, propose features and contribute.

    Release planning board

  • An open community

    Developed in the open in Eclipse Tractus-X, with a regular, public Connector Open Meeting where anyone can ask questions.

    Get help

docs.title: What you get on top of upstream EDC
docs.text:
Upstream EDC on its own Tractus-X EDC Runtime Assemble your own from modules Released runtimes: control plane, data plane and in-memory Container images Build and host your own OSS images on Docker Hub for every release, multi-architecture, non-root Kubernetes Write your own manifests Helm charts with PostgreSQL and Vault options and built-in helm test checks Catena-X policies Write your own policy functions CX-0152 constraints, BPN and BPN group checks, contract definition validation Identity Generic DCP Tested with the Tractus-X Identity Hub and SAP DIV; in Catena-X the BDRS client (BPN ↔ DID) and credential scopes; presentation cache Other dataspaces Assemble from modules A dataspace-agnostic core and dataspace extensions; Factory-X and Construct-X build on it Protocol versions The current DSP version DSP 2025-1 and DSP 0.8 side by side, with connector discovery, so partners on older releases stay reachable Data access EDR building blocks The /v3/edrs API, automatic transfer after negotiation and token refresh Agreements Agreements end with their policy Agreement retirement and the BPNs of both parties stored with each agreement Releases Follow the upstream releases A quarterly release aligned with Eclipse Tractus-X, release candidates tested by QA, pure bugfix releases for the release in use, GitHub milestones Roadmap The upstream project's plans Open planning: features are proposed as issues and planned in public sessions and on the release planning board (how it works) Upgrades Follow upstream release notes Flyway database migrations, a migration guide per release and an upgradeability test in CI Quality and compliance Your own pipeline Deployment, end-to-end and upgradeability tests, CodeQL, Trivy, KICS and secret scans, Eclipse license checks of every dependency Help The EDC community The Connector Open Meeting, a Matrix room, GitHub Discussions, this documentation, the Connector KIT and the Connector Sensei

Not either-or

Tractus-X EDC is EDC: every upstream extension point still works, and you can add your own extensions to the Tractus-X runtimes. See Tutorial 4: your first extension. Fixes and features that are not dataspace specific are meant to go upstream.

docs.title: When upstream EDC alone is the better fit
docs.text:
• You want to assemble every module yourself. For a dataspace with different rules than Catena-X, consider a dataspace extension on Tractus-X EDC first.
  • You work on EDC itself, or on a feature that belongs upstream.

Everyone else, in Catena-X and in other dataspaces, saves time with the released runtimes, images and charts of Tractus-X EDC.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Tractus-X EDC moves data over HTTP out of the box, and the data plane image also contains the upstream EDC extensions for cloud object storage. These guides show how to use them, and where to find extensions for other technologies.

  • Amazon S3

    Offer objects from an S3 bucket and push them to the consumer's bucket (AmazonS3-PUSH), with credentials in the vault or from the pod's IAM role.

    Amazon S3 guide

  • Azure Blob Storage

    Offer blobs from a storage account and push them to the consumer's container (AzureStorage-PUSH), with account keys in the vault and short-lived SAS tokens.

    Azure Blob guide

  • Run on a cloud platform

    Deploy the connector itself on AWS, Azure or another Kubernetes platform.

    Platforms

docs.text:
Technology Transfer type Data address type In the image HTTP HttpData-PULL, HttpData-PUSH HttpData Control and data plane Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage AmazonS3-PUSH AmazonS3 Data plane (data-plane-aws-s3, S3 provisioner), control plane validator Azure Blob Storage AzureStorage-PUSH AzureStorage Data plane (data-plane-azure-storage, blob provisioner)

Each data plane announces the transfer types it supports to the control plane, and the provider's catalog lists them as distribution formats (see Catalog). Mixing works: a provider can serve an S3 asset into an Azure container, and the other way round.

Guides to come

More guides are planned, for example for Google Cloud Storage via its S3-compatible API, MinIO on premises and the Kafka extension. Missing one you need? Open an issue or contribute it.

docs.title: Amazon S3
docs.text:
The data plane of Tractus-X EDC can read objects from an S3 bucket and write them into the consumer's bucket. The transfer type is AmazonS3-PUSH: the provider's data plane copies the data, the consumer only names its destination. Any S3-compatible store (MinIO, Ceph, the S3 API of other clouds) works through endpointOverride.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant CA as Consumer app
  participant CC as Consumer control plane
  participant PC as Provider control plane
  participant PD as Provider data plane
  participant PB as Provider bucket
  participant CB as Consumer bucket
  CA->>CC: Transfer request, AmazonS3-PUSH, destination bucket
  CC->>PC: DSP transfer request
  PC->>PD: Start the data flow
  PD->>PB: Read object(s)
  PD->>CB: Write object(s)
  PD-->>PC: Completed
  PC-->>CC: Transfer completed

docs.title: 1. Credentials
docs.text:
The data plane finds AWS credentials in this order:

Where How Use it for In the data address, by vault reference keyName names a vault secret that holds {"accessKeyId": "…", "secretAccessKey": "…"} (add "sessionToken" for temporary credentials) Recommended for the provider. No secret in the asset. In the data address, inline accessKeyId and secretAccessKey properties Tests and the consumer's destination, which is sent to the provider anyway For the whole data plane dataplane.aws.accessKeyId / dataplane.aws.secretAccessKey in the chart (environment variables AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) One account for all assets From the platform The AWS SDK default chain: IAM role of the pod (IRSA or EKS Pod Identity), instance profile Recommended on EKS. No keys at all.

The consumer's destination credentials reach the provider

The provider's data plane writes into the consumer's bucket, so the destination address, credentials included, goes to the provider. Give the consumer's destination a key that can only write to that bucket or prefix, and rotate it.

docs.title: 2. Provider: offer an object
docs.text:
POST /management/v3/assets HTTP/1.1
Host: provider-controlplane
X-Api-Key: <management API key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "@context": { "@vocab": "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/" },
  "@type": "Asset",
  "@id": "s3-measurements",
  "properties": { "name": "Measurements 2026" },
  "dataAddress": {
    "@type": "DataAddress",
    "type": "AmazonS3",
    "region": "eu-central-1",
    "bucketName": "provider-data",
    "objectName": "measurements/2026.csv",
    "keyName": "s3-provider-data-credentials"
  }
}
Property Meaning region, bucketName Where the data lives. Required. objectName One object. objectPrefix Instead of objectName: every object under this prefix. keyName Vault alias of the credentials (section 1). Leave out to use the data plane's credentials. endpointOverride URL of an S3-compatible store, for example https://minio.example.com.

Store the secret under the alias first, for example in HashiCorp Vault:

vault kv put secret/s3-provider-data-credentials \
  content='{"accessKeyId":"AKIA…","secretAccessKey":"…"}'

The chart's HashiCorp Vault settings are under vault.hashicorp (see Configuration); the secret path and field name depend on them.

Then add a policy and a contract definition as for any asset (tutorial 1). The catalog now offers the dataset with the distribution format AmazonS3-PUSH.

docs.title: 3. Consumer: request the transfer
docs.text:
After the contract negotiation, start the transfer with the agreement and your bucket as destination:

POST /management/v3/transferprocesses HTTP/1.1
Host: consumer-controlplane
X-Api-Key: <management API key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "@context": { "@vocab": "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/" },
  "@type": "TransferRequest",
  "protocol": "dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1",
  "counterPartyAddress": "https://provider.example.com/api/v1/dsp/2025-1",
  "contractId": "<contract agreement id>",
  "transferType": "AmazonS3-PUSH",
  "dataDestination": {
    "@type": "DataAddress",
    "type": "AmazonS3",
    "region": "eu-west-1",
    "bucketName": "consumer-inbox",
    "objectName": "measurements-2026.csv",
    "accessKeyId": "<write-only key id>",
    "secretAccessKey": "<write-only secret>"
  }
}

Use folderName instead of objectName to keep the source names under a folder. Follow the transfer with GET /management/v3/transferprocesses/<id>/state until it is COMPLETED; then the object is in your bucket.

docs.title: 4. Settings
docs.text: Setting Effect dataplane.aws.endpointOverride (EDC_AWS_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE) Default endpoint for all S3 calls, for an S3-compatible store edc.dataplane.aws.sink.chunk.size.mb Size of the parts of a multipart upload into the destination edc.aws.client.async.thread-pool-size Threads of the AWS client

docs.title: Azure Blob Storage
docs.text:
The data plane of Tractus-X EDC can read blobs from an Azure storage account and write them into the consumer's container. The transfer type is AzureStorage-PUSH: the provider's data plane copies the data, the consumer only names its destination.

Unlike S3, no account key leaves its owner: the consumer's connector creates a short-lived, write-only SAS token for its container and sends only that to the provider.

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant CA as Consumer app
  participant CC as Consumer connector
  participant PC as Provider control plane
  participant PD as Provider data plane
  participant PS as Provider storage account
  participant CS as Consumer container
  CA->>CC: Transfer request, AzureStorage-PUSH, destination container
  CC->>CC: Create write-only SAS token from the account key in its vault
  CC->>PC: DSP transfer request with the SAS token
  PC->>PD: Start the data flow
  PD->>PS: Read blob(s) with the provider's account key
  PD->>CS: Write blob(s) with the SAS token
  PD-->>PC: Completed
  PC-->>CC: Transfer completed

docs.title: 1. Keys in the vault
docs.text:
Who Vault secret Value Provider Any alias, named in the asset's keyName The storage account key of the source account Consumer The name of the storage account The storage account key of the destination account

The storage account keys never appear in the Management API.

docs.title: 2. Provider: offer a blob
docs.text:
POST /management/v3/assets HTTP/1.1
Host: provider-controlplane
X-Api-Key: <management API key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "@context": { "@vocab": "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/" },
  "@type": "Asset",
  "@id": "blob-measurements",
  "properties": { "name": "Measurements 2026" },
  "dataAddress": {
    "@type": "DataAddress",
    "type": "AzureStorage",
    "account": "providerdata",
    "container": "measurements",
    "blobName": "2026.csv",
    "keyName": "providerdata-key"
  }
}
Property Meaning account, container Where the data lives. Required. blobName One blob. blobPrefix Instead of blobName: every blob under this prefix, for example folder/. keyName Vault alias of the account key (section 1). Required.

Add a policy and a contract definition as for any asset (tutorial 1). The catalog now offers the dataset with the distribution format AzureStorage-PUSH.

docs.title: 3. Consumer: request the transfer
docs.text:
After the contract negotiation:

POST /management/v3/transferprocesses HTTP/1.1
Host: consumer-controlplane
X-Api-Key: <management API key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "@context": { "@vocab": "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/" },
  "@type": "TransferRequest",
  "protocol": "dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1",
  "counterPartyAddress": "https://provider.example.com/api/v1/dsp/2025-1",
  "contractId": "<contract agreement id>",
  "transferType": "AzureStorage-PUSH",
  "dataDestination": {
    "@type": "DataAddress",
    "type": "AzureStorage",
    "account": "consumerinbox",
    "container": "incoming",
    "folderName": "measurements"
  }
}

The container must exist. folderName is optional: without it, the blobs land at the top of the container with their source names. Follow the transfer with GET /management/v3/transferprocesses/<id>/state until it is COMPLETED.

docs.title: 4. Settings
docs.text:
Setting Effect edc.blobstore.endpoint.template Endpoint of the blob service, %s stands for the account name. Default: https://%s.blob.core.windows.net. Set it for Azurite or sovereign clouds. edc.azure.block.size.mb, edc.azure.max.concurrency, edc.azure.max.single.upload.size.mb Upload tuning of the data plane

Set them as environment variables in dataplane.env (and controlplane.env for the endpoint template), see Configuration.

docs.title: Solution 1: Update all Criteria manually
docs.text:
Root of this issue is that the operator, left- and right-operand Criteria field names changed.

Old New left operandLeft right operandRight op operator

It is possible to resolve this issue by updating the content of the column, that contain JSON serialized constraints, from

{"criteria":[{"left":"asset:prop:id","op":"=","right":"asset-1"}]}

to

{"criteria":[{"operandLeft":"asset:prop:id","operator":"=","operandRight":"asset-1"}]}

docs.title: Solution 2: Delete all rows containing Constraints
docs.text:
Instead of updating each row in the database it's also possible to delete all Contract Definitions and Policies. Additionally it's necessary to delete all Negotiations, as they might reference existing Contract Definitions and/or Policies.

Theoretically it's also necessary to delete Contract Agreements. As their deletion is already described in another section, we can skip them here.

docs.title: Required Queries
docs.text:
DELETE
FROM edc_contract_negotiation;

DELETE
FROM edc_contract_definitions;

DELETE
FROM edc_policydefinitins;

docs.title: 1.2 Delete Contract Agreements
docs.text: In the new version contract agreement rows contain a serialized policy at the time, the contract was concluded. With the EDC update all existing Contract Agreements must be deleted.

docs.title: Required Query
docs.text:
DELETE
FROM edc_contract_agreement;

docs.title: 2. Data Management API
docs.text: It might be necessary to update applications and scripts that use the Data Management API. This section covers the most important changes in endpoints and payloads.

docs.title: 2.1 Policy Path
docs.text: The Data Management API Path for Policies changes from /policies to /policydefinitions.

docs.title: Get All Policies
docs.text: curl -X GET "${DATA_MGMT_ENDPOINT}/data/policydefinitions" --header "X-Api-Key: <key>" --header "Content-Type: application/json"

docs.title: 2.2 Policy Payload
docs.text: The Policy Payload now wraps the policy details in an additional policy object.

docs.title: New Payload
docs.text:
{
  "uid": "1",
  "policy": {
    "prohibitions": [],
    "obligations": [],
    "permissions": []
  }
}

docs.title: Old Payload
docs.text:
{
  "uid": "1",
  "prohibitions": [],
  "obligations": [],
  "permissions": []
}

docs.title: 2.3 Criteria in Payload of Contract Definitions and Policies
docs.text: The payload of a Policy or a Contract Definition may contain one or more Criteria. The format of these serialized Criteria changed. Please note that there is no input validation, that detects errors when the old Criteria format is used!

docs.title: Old Criterion Format
docs.text: { "left": "asset:prop:id", "op": "=", "right": "1" }

docs.title: New Criterion Format
docs.text: { "operandLeft": "asset:prop:id", "operator": "=", "operandRight": "1" }

docs.title: Example Call
docs.text: curl -X POST "${DATA_MGMT_ENDPOINT}/data/contractdefinitions" --header "X-Api-Key: <key>" --header "Content-Type: application/json" --data "{ \"id\": \"1\", \"criteria\": [ { \"operandLeft\": \"asset:prop:id\", \"operator\": \"=\", \"operandRight\": \"1\" } ], \"accessPolicyId\": \"1\", \"contractPolicyId\": \"1\" }"

docs.title: 2.4 Data Address
docs.text: When using a Data Address of type HttpData please notice that the property endpoint changed to baseUrl. This property is mostly used when creating assets.

docs.title: Old Asset format
docs.text:
{
  "asset": {
    ...
  },
  "dataAddress": {
    "properties": {
      "endpoint": "http://provider-backend-service:8080/data/asset-1",
      "type": "HttpData"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: New Asset format
docs.text:
{
  "asset": {
    ...
  },
  "dataAddress": {
    "properties": {
      "baseUrl": "http://provider-backend-service:8080/data/asset-1",
      "type": "HttpData"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Example Call
docs.text: curl -X POST "$PLATO_DATAMGMT_URL/data/assets" --header "X-Api-Key: password" --header "Content-Type: application/json" --data "{ \"asset\": { \"properties\": { \"asset:prop:id\": \"1\", \"asset:prop:description\": \"Tractus-X EDC Demo Asset\" } }, \"dataAddress\": { \"properties\": { \"type\": \"HttpData\", \"baseUrl\": \"https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1\" } } }" -s -o /dev/null -w 'Response Code: %{http_code}\n'

docs.title: 3.1 Token Validation Endpoint Setting
docs.text: In the past the token validation endpoint was configured in edc.controlplane.validation-endpoint. This setting key must be renamed to edc.dataplane.token.validation.endpoint.

docs.title: 3.2 DataPlane Selector
docs.text: With this version a new feature was introduced which allows to have separate DataPlane instances for different transfer-flows (HttpProxy, S3, etc.). The Tractus-X EDC also has a new extension which allows for a simpler registration of additional dataplanes. Further documentation can be found in the extension folder: dataplane-selector-configuration

docs.title: Migration Version 0.1.0 to 0.1.1
docs.text:
This document contains a list of breaking changes that are introduced in version 0.1.1.

Please Note: Due to a change in the DAPS authentication mechanism this version cannot exchange messages with older EDC versions!

docs.title: 0. Summary
docs.text:
1. Data Management API
  2. Policy Payload
  3. Connector Configuration
  4. CX OAuth Extension

docs.title: 1. Data Management API
docs.text: It might be necessary to update applications and scripts that use the Data Management API. This section covers the most important changes in endpoints and payloads.

docs.title: 1.1 Policy Payload
docs.text: The id field of the PolicyDefinition was renamed from uid to id.

docs.title: Old Call
docs.text:
{
    "uid": "1",
    "policy": {
        "prohibitions": [],
        "obligations": [],
        "permissions": [
            {
                "edctype": "dataspaceconnector:permission",
                "action": {
                    "type": "USE"
                },
                "constraints": []
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: New call
docs.text:
{
    "id": "1",
    "policy": {
        "prohibitions": [],
        "obligations": [],
        "permissions": [
            {
                "edctype": "dataspaceconnector:permission",
                "action": {
                    "type": "USE"
                },
                "constraints": []
            }
        ]
    }
}

docs.title: 2.1. CX OAuth Extension
docs.text:
All connectors are now shipped with a new OAuth extension. This extension has an additional mandatory setting called edc.ids.endpoint.audience, that must be set to the IDS path.

Documentation

docs.title: Example
docs.text: edc.ids.endpoint.audience=http://plato-edc-controlplane:8282/api/v1/ids/data

docs.title: Migration Version 0.1.2 to 0.1.3
docs.text: This document contains a list of breaking changes that are introduced in version 0.1.3.

docs.title: OAuth2 Extension
docs.text:
As the images now use the official OAuth2 Extension, the audience settings need to the updated.

Add the following settings:

  • EDC_OAUTH_PROVIDER_AUDIENCE
  • EDC_OAUTH_ENDPOINT_AUDIENCE

Remove the following setting:

  • EDC_IDS_ENDPOINT_AUDIENCE

Example:

EDC_OAUTH_PROVIDER_AUDIENCE: idsc:IDS_CONNECTORS_ALL
EDC_OAUTH_ENDPOINT_AUDIENCE: http://plato-edc-controlplane:8282/api/v1/ids/data

docs.title: Deprecation
docs.text: • the edc-controlplane and edc-dataplane charts are deprecated, please use tractusx-connector which combines the former ones

docs.title: Management API changes
docs.text:
Details at the official documentation on swaggerhub

  • Management API for creating resources (assets, policydefinitions, contractdefinitions, ...) will return a body containing the id of the created resource
  • Added a POST /request for every management endpoint (assets, policydefinitions, ...) to query all the resources. The existent GET / have been deprecated
  • added id field in DataRequestDTO (/transferprocess management api), if not set it will use a randomly generated one.
  • Removed field assetId from ContractOffer. It was always null though, so there should be nothing to do about it.
  • on POST /contractdefinitions a duration field can be added to control the duration of the contract.
  • added the GET /assets/{id}/address endpoint to being able to retrieve the stored DataAddress

docs.title: Settings changes
docs.text:
• refactored the HTTP server contexts (more details on the related decision record). They need to be refactored as:
  • web.http.data becomes web.http.management
  • web.http.ids becomes web.http.protocol
  • web.http.validation, web.http.controlplane and web.http.dataplane become web.http.control
  • Healthcheck api now it's exposed under the management context.
  • Removed default value for setting edc.transfer.proxy.token.verifier.publickey.alias so it must be valued accordingly
  • made the state machine settings configurable so it will be possible to tune them accordingly. More details in the related documentation entry.
  • renamed edc.receiver.http.endpoint to edc.receiver.http.dynamic.endpoint
  • renamed edc.oauth.public.key.alias setting to edc.oauth.certificate.alias

docs.title: Other changes
docs.text:
• Supported /public data plane endpoint without trailing slash, that can be eventually removed from the configuration
  • packages name changed from org.eclipse.dataspaceconnector to org.eclipse.edc
  • To specify multiple BPN into Policies the operator OR can be used. More details in the business-partner-validation extension documentation
  • HTTP Dynamic Endpoint Data Reference: The URL for Endpoint Data Reference can be also provided via the call for starting the transfer process. More details Http Dynamic EDR receiver

docs.title: Observability API changes
docs.text: All endpoints (/health, /startup, /liveness, /readiness) of the Observability API now support unauthenticated access, if configured. That will put the Observability API under a new context named "observability", which consequently requires proper web context configuration for it. Note that the name of the context cannot be changed.

docs.title: Settings changes
docs.text:
• tractusx.api.observability.allow-insecure: boolean value that enables (true) the unauthenticated access.
  • web.http.observability.port: integer value that specifies the port of the observability context. Mandatory if unauthenticated access is enabled!
  • web.http.observability.path: string value that specifies the path of the observability context. Mandatory if unauthenticated access is enabled!

docs.title: Configuration of Azure KeyVault
docs.text:
When using Helm Charts that use the Azure KeyVault (edc-runtime-memory, edc-controlplane-postgres) it is now possible to select either authentication via Client Secret (azure.vault.secret) or via certificate (azure.vault.certificate).

If neither of the two is configured, the runtime will fail to start issuing an error.

docs.title: Refactoring of Helm Charts
docs.text:
In issue #136 work has begun to split the Helm charts up into several technology-focused charts:

  • In-memory: for testing and development
  • PostgreSQL+Hashicorp: this is the recommended distribution of Tractus-X EDC
  • (Azure KeyVault: uses Azure KeyVault instead of Hashicorp Vault.) - Work in Progress

Unfortunately, due to time constraints, we had to release 0.3.4 without the Azure KeyVault chart, it will be included in one of the subsequent releases in the future.

Please note that the Azure KeyVault variant is not included in the 0.3.4 Release! If you rely on AZKV please do NOT upgrade to 0.3.4 yet!

docs.title: Change in Docker image publishing
docs.text: Starting with the 0.3.3 release we switched over to publish our Docker images to Docker Hub instead of GHCR.

docs.title: Switching to DSP
docs.text:
The Eclipse Dataspace Connector protocol recently moved its protocol implementation from IDS to DSP as of version 0.0.1-milestone-9. From the Tractus-X EDC perspective this causes breaking changes in the following areas:

  • the Management API: because DSP uses JSON-LD, all Management API endpoints had to be adapted as well to reflect that. The old Management API is now deprecated and is not tested for compliance. Please upgrade using the /v2/ path for every endpoint, e.g. <PATH>/management/v2/assets. Please also refer to the EDC OpenAPI spec. An updated postman collection with the v2 flow is available here

  • modules: all *ids* modules are deprecated and cannot be used anymore. Please migrate over to org.eclipse.edc:dsp:0.0.1-milestone-9.

  • path: the default protocol path is now /api/v1/dsp instead of /api/v1/ids

  • edc.participant.id: new mandatory configuration for the participant id in the dataspace (BPN number). It's configured via mandatory property in the charts with object yaml participant: id: "id".

Please note that this is not a complete documentation of the DSP Protocol, please refer to the official documentation

docs.title: Removal of the Business Tests
docs.text:
The business tests were removed from the code base, because all the ever tested is already by other tests, specifically the JUnit-based tests, deployment tests, or other tests that are already done upstream in EDC.

The Business tests were brittle, consumed a lot of resources and were quite cumbersome to run and debug locally.

docs.title: New implementation for the Control Plane Adapter
docs.text: Since the old Control-Plane-Adapter is incompatible with DSP, a new iteration was created. Due to time constraints with this release documentation for this feature will to be published subsequently

docs.title: New Policies for expressing validity of the agreement
docs.text: The dates in ContractOffer and ContractAgreement has been removed in favour of a policy based contract validity check, see here

docs.title: Other changes
docs.text:
• When using the EDR HttpDynamicReceiverExtension in the transfer process initiation the properties for configuring the receiver on single transfer process has been changed to:
"privateProperties": {
      "receiverHttpEndpoint": "{{BACKEND_SERVICE}}"
}

instead of:

"properties": {
      "receiver.http.endpoint": "{{BACKEND_SERVICE}}"
}

docs.title: New Catalog
docs.text:
The DSP catalog is expressed as DCat Catalog, when querying the catalog a response like this will return:

{
    "@id": "5a3207ae-bd0d-4a3b-bc8a-05adfbe75d95",
    "@type": "dcat:Catalog",
    "dcat:dataset": {
        "@id": "e6279569-17a9-4ba3-9401-a8ae4100e4eb",
        "@type": "dcat:Dataset",
        "odrl:hasPolicy": {
            "@id": "2:1:535def6e-8321-4c0e-a595-aabdd9c18eed",
            "@type": "odrl:Set",
            "odrl:permission": [],
            "odrl:prohibition": [],
            "odrl:obligation": [],
            "odrl:target": "1"
        },
        "dcat:distribution": [
         ...
        ],
        "edc:description": "Product EDC Demo Asset",
        "edc:id": "1"
    },
    "dcat:service": {
      ...
    },
    "edc:participantId": "participantId",
    "@context": {
    }
}

When starting a new contract negotiation for an asset:

  • the @id of odrl:hasPolicy object should be passed in the offerId field
  • the edc:participantId should be passed in the providerId and connectorId fields. connectorId it's still needed for backward compatibility and it will probably be removed in the next versions.

docs.title: Replacing DAPS with SSI
docs.text: DAPS was deprecated as identity provider, and was replaced with an Self-Sovereign-Identity solution based on a centralized Managed Identity Wallet (MIW) using VerifiableCredentials. Initially, there will be one SummaryCredential, which conflates all relevant information. This is intended as interim solution and will later be replaced with a more appropriate structure.

docs.title: Relevant terminology
docs.text:
Please make sure to be at least somewhat familiar with the following terms before you read on:

  • VerifiableCredential
  • VerifiablePresentation
  • JWT - JSON Web Token
  • DSP - the DataSpace Protocol

docs.title: Preconditions
docs.text:
All of these preconditions must be met before Tractus-X EDC v0.5.x is usable in a production use case. Please read them carefully and make sure you understand the implications.

  • every connector instance must have a signed SummaryCredential sitting in the MIW. This is typically done by the Portal during participant onboarding.
  • the connector must have an account with KeyCloak and be able to obtain access tokens.
  • the connector must be able to reach both MIW and KeyCloak via HTTP

docs.title: Authentication flow - quick intro
docs.text:
The basic workflow for a connector runtime to authenticate an incoming request is described in this section. Please note that this procedure is limited to connector-to-connector communication via the Dataspace Protocol (DSP), it does not relate to other APIs such as the Management API.

When a request is made by the Consumer, it obtains an access token from KeyCloak, which it uses to authenticate to MIW. It then requests its SummaryCredential from MIW, which is returned in the form of a signed JWT that contains a VerifiablePresentation (VP). That JWT is attached to the outgoing request as authorization header. The Provider then decodes the JWT, validates its claims, and then uploads the VP to MIW for verification. Upon successful verification, the Provider proceeds to process the request.

Please also check out this flow diagram and the associated documentation.

docs.title: Connecting to MIW
docs.text:
For connector onboarding, please contact the Portal Team. After that, you should receive:

  • the issuer BPN: this is the BPN of the MIW
  • your client id: this is the KeyCloak Client ID
  • your client secret: this the KeyCloak Client Secret. Please store this in a secure vault and remember the alias. Do not leak or publish this!

In order to establish a connection to MIW, and you are using EDC on code level, please be sure to follow this documentation. If you are using the official Helm charts, please check out this documentation.

If you are using the MIW and KeyCloak instances deployed to INT, the following values apply:

  • MIW Url: https://managed-identity-wallets-new.int.demo.catena-x.net
  • KeyCloak Token URL: https://centralidp.int.demo.catena-x.net/auth/realms/CX-Central/protocol/openid-connect/token
  • Authority BPN: BPNL00000003CRHK

Please be aware that the above values are only valid for the Catena-X INT environment and will change on other environments! For instructions on how to set up a local MIW + KeyCloak, please take a look at this documentation.

docs.title: Further documentation on SSI
docs.text: Please find more information in the SSI Documentation Repository.

docs.title: Noteworthy things and Caveats
docs.text:
• the MIWs REST API is secured with a token that can be obtained from a KeyCloak instance. This KeyCloak instance must be configured appropriately ahead of time.
  • connectors have to be able to obtain a token from KeyCloak, so it must have an account with that KeyCloak instance
  • we do not ship either MIW or KeyCloak nor do we provide support for either of them. Please contact the respective Tractus-X projects for instructions how to set them up.
  • our official Helm charts now use SSI instead of DAPS. However, the charts do not include a dependency onto MIW of KeyCloak, nor do they contain configuration for them. They do, however, contain a configuration section (titled ssi) that configures EDC.
  • our Helm charts can be installed, and the connector application will boot up, but unless MIW and KeyCloak are configured properly and both can be reached over network by the connector, every DSP request to another connector will fail. However, the ManagementAPI can still be used to create Assets, Policies and ContractDefinitions.
  • At the time of releasing Tractus-X EDC 0.5.0, a couple of critical issues regarding MIW are still in progress, and the code base is still on a feature branch. For those reasons we recommend to use non-production data only!
  • the centralized MIW is an interim solution, and is bound to be replaced with a decentralized/distributed architecture in upcoming Catena-X releases.

docs.title: The Observability API changes
docs.text:
The following settings are removed because the observability-api-customization extension will be no longer used. The Observability API extension will be used instead

  • observability.port
  • observability.path
  • observability.insecure

The status (/health, /startup, /liveness, /readiness) of the EDC can be checked by using the default endpoint.

docs.title: The Consumer Pull flow changes
docs.text:
Starting from 0.5.0-rc5 which incorporates EDC 0.1.3, the consumer pull has been simplified in upstream, and it can cause some breaking changes on users usage. The change is reflected in this diagram.

The main difference is that in the previous iteration of the pull flow there were two EDRs involved. One created by the provider while serving a transfer request, and one created by the consumer (wrapping the provider one). The consumer one then was dispatched to the EDR receivers for requesting the data via consumer dataplane.

In the current iteration the receivers now receive directly the provider EDR without the double "wrapping" and can be used directly to fetch data from the provider dataplane, without passing thought to the consumer dataplane.

The shape of the EDR has not been changed so, if in the backend systems the EDR#endpoint was used as url for fetching data, it should not cause any breaking changes.

If the backend system manually forward the EDR to the consumer dataplane or tries to decode it via consumer validate token APIs, this will not work with signature check errors, as the EDR is the one signed by the provider.

Note the custom property cid in the EDR, it's not available anymore. The property it's still available inside the JWT authCode

docs.title: 1.1 Overview
docs.text:
Dataplane Signaling effectively replaces the previous data plane public API. It is a standardized way for the control plane to communicate with the data plane, e.g. when suspending or resuming data transfers.

New features like token renewal build on top of it.

This replaces the Control API, the Public API and the EDR callbacks

docs.title: 1.2 Automatic token renewal
docs.text:
When a TransferProcess enters the STARTED state, the consumer connector receives the Endpoint Data Reference (EDR) that contains the URL to the public API, an access token, a refresh token and endpoint where the token can be refreshed.

EDRs are now cached automatically within the consumer connector's control plane, and the EDR API will auto-refresh the token if it is nearing expiry.

docs.title: 1.3 New data format for DataAddress
docs.text: In order for Dataplane Signaling to become aligned with the Dataspace Protocol (DSP), DataAddress objects now conform to the dspace data format.

docs.title: 1.4 Dataplane Signaling API
docs.text: This is a new REST api that replaces the old Control API for a more consolidated and streamlined communication between a participant's control plane and data plane.

docs.title: 1.5 Configuration values
docs.text: Helm value Environment value required default value description dataplane.token.refresh.expiry_seconds TX_EDC_DATAPLANE_TOKEN_EXPIRY 30 TTL for access tokens dataplane.token.refresh.expiry_tolerance_seconds TX_EDC_DATAPLANE_TOKEN_EXPIRY_TOLERANCE 10 tolerance for token expiry dataplane.token.refresh.refresh_endpoint TX_EDC_DATAPLANE_TOKEN_REFRESH_ENDPOINT <PUBLIC_API>/token endpoint for an OAuth2 token refresh request dataplane.token.signer.privatekey_alias EDC_TRANSFER_PROXY_TOKEN_SIGNER_PRIVATEKEY_ALIAS x alias, under which the private key is stored in the vault dataplane.token.verifier.publickey_alias EDC_TRANSFER_PROXY_TOKEN_VERIFIER_PUBLICKEY_ALIAS x alias, under which the public key is stored in the vault
