docs.text:
• Dataplane Signaling documentation and token handling
  • Tractus-X Specification for Token Renewal
  • Tractus-X EDC Implementation Documentation

docs.title: 2. Changes to EDR handling and APIs
docs.text:
The setting backendService.httpProxyTokenReceiverUrl, which configured an EDR receiver backend using the upstream EDC extension is no longer available as well as the extension is not shipped in the Tractus-X EDC 0.7.x distributions. Likewise, the option to dynamically register a consumer-side HTTP-callback via receiverHttpEndpoint in the POST /transferprocesses call was removed. Consumer apps should use the /v2/edrs API instead.

The main reason is that EDC/Tractus-X-EDC switched to Dataplane Signaling for handling transfers and the EDR format specified in DPS spec was not handled properly by the receiver extension.

Now all the EDRs are automatically stored by the consumer's EDR cache and made available via the new EDRs API. If users still need to receive the EDR on their backend and want to process this manually, EDC can handle this natively by registering an HTTP callback for the transfer.process.start event.

This can be done in two ways:

  • dynamic callbacks (associated to each transfer process)
  • static callbacks (configured at boot time)

docs.title: 2.1 Example of dynamic callback
docs.text:
When starting a new transfer process callbackAddresses can be attached to the transfer request:

{
  "callbackAddresses": [
    {
      "events": [
        "transfer.process.started"
      ],
      "uri": "https://mybackend/edr"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 2.2 Example of static callbacks configuration
docs.text:
EDC_CALLBACK_CB1_URI="https://mybackend/edr"
EDC_CALLBACK_CB1_EVENTS="transfer.process.started"

When configuring static callbacks like above, users will receive notifications about transfer process start events of both sides consumer/provider if the connector acts as both. This can be checked by the type property in the event itself.

Users need to be aware that if they handle the receiver manually, they also have to handle EDR token refresh using either the EDR API or by manually calling the refresh endpoint (not recommended).

docs.title: 2.3 References
docs.text:
• OpenAPI Spec, "Control Plane EDR Api"
  • More info about callbacks

docs.title: 3. Identity And Trust Protocols (IATP)
docs.text:
IATP defines the message flow between a consumer connector and a provider connector when they want to exchange DSP messages. On every message exchange, the recipient asks the sender for certain VerifiableCredentials, which are accessed from the sender's credential storage (= "wallet").

In this release, the only IATP-compliant wallet is a centrally hosted commercial solution provided by SAP called "DIM". Here, the DIM wallet acts as both a Secure Token Service (STS), a CredentialService (CS) and a server for DID documents.

This setup replaces the Managed Identity Wallet.

docs.title: 3.1 Preconditions
docs.text:
During participant onboarding the following information is generated/disclosed and must be configured before launching the connector.

  • DIM client ID: during onboarding a Client ID is created, which represents the participant's tenant within DIM
  • DIM client secret: similarly, the Client Secret authenticates the tenant with DIM. The actual secret must be stored under this alias in the participant's vault (Hashicorp Vault: secrets/<ALIAS>)!
  • DIM token URL: connectors must use this URL to request access tokens using their client-ID and client secret to obtain an access token for DIM
  • DIM STS URL: this is the URL where connectors can request self-issued ID tokens. This is needed for every DSP request, and when querying the BDRS.
  • Decentralized Identifier (DID): the DID is a unique identifier that exposes public information such as service endpoints or public key material. This DID is generated by DIM upon registration.

docs.title: 3.2 Configuration values
docs.text: Helm value Environment value required default value description iatp.id EDC_IAM_ISSUER_ID x DID, e.g. did:web:your connector iatp.trustedIssuers EDC_IAM_TRUSTED-ISSUER_{{$index}}-ISSUER_ID x a list of DIDs, each representing an issuer of VCs iatp.sts.dim.url TX_EDC_IAM_STS_DIM_URL x URL where connectors can request SI tokens iatp.sts.oauth.token_url EDC_IAM_STS_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL x URL where connectors can request OAuth2 access tokens for DIM iatp.sts.oauth.client.id EDC_IAM_STS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID x Client ID issued by DIM iatp.sts.oauth.client.secret_alias EDC_IAM_STS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET_ALIAS x alias under which the client secret is stored in the vault

docs.title: 3.3 DIDs and BPNs
docs.text:
In Tractus-X, BusinessPartnerNumbers (BPNs) are unique, stable identifiers that identify participants within the network. IATP relies on Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs), which are used to dereference information about the participant such as service endpoints, public key material, etc.

Since there is no way to implicitly map BPN <> DID, Tractus-X relies on a new core service called "BPN/DID Resolution Service" ("BDRS"), which provides that mapping information to authenticated parties.

docs.title: 3.4 References
docs.text:
• IATP Specification
  • Tractus-X Credentials
  • Tractus-X Policies

docs.title: 3.5 Limitations
docs.text: • It is not possible to define an access policy that would require the evaluation of a VerifiableCredential

docs.title: 4. BPN/DID Resolution Service
docs.text:
The BPN/DID Resolution Service (BDRS) is a new core service that became necessary due to the dual use of identifiers ( BPNs and DIDs) in Catena-X.

In short, it exposes a GZipped list of BPN<>DID tuples, which the connector caches locally and updates periodically. This API is called the Directory API.

These requests are authenticated by putting the participant's MembershipCredential in the Authorization header.

docs.title: 4.1 Config values
docs.text: Helm value Environment value required default value description controlplane.bdrs.cache_validity_seconds TX_IAM_IATP_BDRS_CACHE_VALIDITY 600 time (sec) that the client cache is valid controlplane.bdrs.server.url TX_IAM_IATP_BDRS_SERVER_URL x base URL of the BDRS server

docs.title: 4.2 References
docs.text:
• BDRS Server on GitHub
  • BDRS Server Directory API
  • BDRS Server Management API ( not for public consumption)

Further, the BDRS server is available as Helm chart from the official Tractus-X Chart Repo:

  • bdrs-server: official distribution using Postgres
  • bdrs-server-memory: variant, that uses pure in-mem storage, useful for testing

To see how BDRS could be used in testing/dev etc. check out this test class

Note that consuming the Directory API with tools like Postman or Insomnia is possible, but not straight forward and it is out-of-scope for this document.

docs.title: 5.0 Policies
docs.text:
Due to #4192 and #4179

The action and the leftOperand field are now represented as @id instead of value in JSON-LD.

action from:

 {
  "odrl:permission": {
    "odrl:action": {
      "odrl:type": "http://www.w3.org/ns/odrl/2/use"
    }
  }
}

to:

{
  "odrl:action": {
    "@id": "odrl:use"
  }
}

leftOperand from:

{
  "odrl:leftOperand": "https://w3id.org/catenax/policy/FrameworkAgreement"
}

to:

{
  "odrl:leftOperand": {
    "@id": "cx-policy:FrameworkAgreement"
  }
}

This is reflected in the Catalog as well as in PolicyDefinition API.

docs.title: 5.1 Catalog
docs.text: • counterPartyId is a required property for the catalog request in Tractus-X EDC. It's not enforced currently ( backward compatibility) but if not provided, the IATP flows won't work and thus the catalog request will fail.

docs.title: 5.2 Transfer Process
docs.text: • transferType is a needed property for the transfer request to be working in tx-edc. transferTypes are the supported transfer format in tx-edc. They return as part of the Catalog response as part of distribution format for an asset. In TX-EDC we currently supports HttpData-PULL, AzureStorage-PUSH and AmazonS3-PUSH. The transferType is not mandatory (backward compatibility) but if not provided the transfer request will fail.

docs.title: 5.3 EDRs
docs.text:
The 0.5.4 EDRs API was removed due the adoption of DPS (data plane signaling) and reborn under a different shape in /v2/edrs

The main difference between 0.5.4 and 0.7.0 is how the token refresh is handled. In 0.5.x when an EDR was about to expire, the users had to manually trigger another transfer process, or use the EDR API which did that automatically. This approach had major drawbacks like proactively creating transfer process on EDR expiration. In 0.7.0 this changed radically by adopting DPS and overlaying on top of it a refresh mechanism for EDRs.

For a detailed explanation, please refer to the EDR API documentation.

docs.title: 6. Other changes and noteworthy items
docs.text:
• Changes in the policy definition properties: A policy definition now adheres to ODRL and the @type has changed to Set
  • An Offer does not contain a target property anymore, it has to be injected in the ContractRequest message.
  • The consumerId and providerId were replaced by the ODRL assigneeand assigner, respectively. The latter also has to be injected in the ContractRequest Message.
  • A transfer process has now a new transfer type property that should adhere to the following mapping: https://github.com/eclipse-edc/Connector/blob/v0.7.2/docs/developer/data-plane-signaling/data-plane-signaling-mapping.md
  • The EDR API changed, and it's no longer possible to query for EDRs by contract agreement directly. A QuerySpec with a filter has to be used for this.
  • The AWS S3 Extension also has been improved and now enables the user to specify S3 object prefixes in the data address. This enables the transfer of multiple files within on single transfer process. For more information, visit the extension readme.
  • contrary to previous deprecation warnings, the Business Partner Number evaluation function will remain in place and can continue to be used in parallel to the Business Partner Group evaluation function.
  • changes to environment variables in the Azure KeyVault variant of Tractus-X EDC. Note that this does not affect the Helm config values.
    • EDC_VAULT_CLIENTID was replaced by AZURE_CLIENT_ID
    • EDC_VAULT_TENANTID was replaced by AZURE_TENANT_ID
    • EDC_VAULT_CLIENTSECRET was replaced by AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
    • EDC_VAULT_CERTIFICATE was replaced by AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH

docs.title: Migration Guide 0.7.x -> 0.8.x
docs.text:
Note: this guide is still work in progress, if you have some additional feedback to give, please use the related discussion: https://github.com/eclipse-tractusx/tractusx-edc/discussions/1579

  • Migration Guide 0.7.x -> 0.8.x
  • 1. New datasource configuration
  • 2. New SQL schema migrations
    • 2.1. Control plane:
    • 2.2. Data plane:
  • 3. Deprecation cleanup
  • 4. New Contract Agreements Retirement Feature
  • 5. Application program arguments
    • 5.1. Changing Log Level via TractusX helm charts

docs.title: 1. New datasource configuration
docs.text:
So far the SQL datasource configuration was 1:1 with the "store context" one, so the EDC forced to use a dedicated datasource for every store, now the two concepts are separated, so by default there will be a single default datasource defined in the Helm Chart and by default all the stores will use that.

So, if you are not using the provided Tractus-X Helm Charts and you don't need to use different datasources for different stores, we suggest to remove all the edc.datasource.<xxx> settings and leave just the edc.datasource.default settings group. If you use the Tractus-X EDC Helm Charts there is no further action required on your part.

In any case please follow the advice given by the WARNING log messages in the EDC console output.

Ref. https://eclipse-edc.github.io/documentation/for-contributors/postgres-persistence/

docs.title: 2. New SQL schema migrations
docs.text: For those who are not using either the Helm Charts or the provided migration modules:

docs.title: 2.1. Control plane:
docs.text:
• contract negotiation- create state index
  • data plane instance - init schema
  • federated catalog - init schema
  • policy monitor - create state index
  • policy definition - add profiles column
  • WARNING: When upgrading from 0.7.X, if your policy definition table already has data, this migration will lead the PolicyDefinitionStore to throw runtime errors. As a workaround you can manually run the query contained in the subsequent migration. The migration fix will be available from 0.8.1 on.
  • transfer process - create state index

docs.title: 2.2. Data plane:
docs.text:
• dataplane - add transfer type destination column
  • dataplane - create state index

docs.title: 3. Deprecation cleanup
docs.text:
There were many deprecations deleted after some time, mostly regarding spis, something about configuration settings. Management API didn't change, we're still using upstream version 3.

If you noticed and took care of everything that was logged as WARNING (which we strongly recommend) you shouldn't find any other difficulties.

docs.title: 4. New Contract Agreements Retirement Feature
docs.text:
A new extension was added that allows a dataspace participant to prematurely retire an active contract agreement. Once a contract agreement is retired, all existing transfer processes will be terminated. New transfer process requests, using the retired contract agreement, will also fail to start.

The extension adds a set of API endpoints that allow the dataspace participant to manage its retired contract agreements. API details can be found in the OpenAPI specification.

Further details about the extension can be found in the extension README file.

docs.title: 5. Application program arguments
docs.text:
When using the distributed tractusx-edc docker images, you can now specify program arguments that will change how the Connector behaves. Example:

docker run edc-runtime-memory:0.8.0 --no-color

The supported program arguments and their behavior are:

  • Removing the coloring option of the default Console Monitor logs by using the program argument --no-color.
  • Changing the Connectors' default Console Monitor log levels by using the program argument --log-level=WARNING. Possible log levels are [SEVERE, WARNING, INFO, DEBUG].

docs.title: 5.1. Changing Log Level via TractusX helm charts
docs.text:
If you use the TractusX helm charts, you can change the log level of the default Console Monitor by changing the logs.level configuration in values.yml of you chart (example below). The default level is set as DEBUG by default.

https://github.com/eclipse-tractusx/tractusx-edc/blob/03df535b822f7e6430032feb3775280e123b03cc/charts/tractusx-connector-memory/values.yaml#L77-L79

The old log level configurations were removed (below), as they were not used by the connector in any way and could induce the user of the helm charts in error.

#-- configuration of the [Java Util Logging Facade](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/technotes/guides/logging/overview.html)
-logging: |-
-.level=INFO
-org.eclipse.edc.level=ALL
-handlers=java.util.logging.ConsoleHandler
-java.util.logging.ConsoleHandler.formatter=java.util.logging.SimpleFormatter
-java.util.logging.ConsoleHandler.level=ALL
-java.util.logging.SimpleFormatter.format=[%1$tY-%1$tm-%1$td %1$tH:%1$tM:%1$tS] [%4$-7s] %5$s%6$s%n

docs.title: Migration Guide 0.8.x -> 0.9.x
docs.text:
This document outlines the necessary changes for migrating your tractusx-edc installation from version 0.8.0 to 0.9.0. It also outlines some points that adopters and operators should pay close attention to when migrating from one version to another.

This document is not a comprehensive feature list.

  • Migration Guide 0.8.x -> 0.9.x
  • 1. Strict Policy Definition Validation
  • 2. Removal of Azure based distributions
  • 3. Updated and Deprecated BPNL Group operators
  • 4. Store Migrations

docs.title: 1. Strict Policy Definition Validation
docs.text:
A new feature was added with upstream EDC 0.11.0 that requires the connector to perform a deeper validation of a policy definition during its creation/update. This feature prevents any new policy definition of having:

  • an action, within a rule, that doesn't bound to any evaluation scope
  • a constraint, within a rule, that its leftOperand is not bound to any evaluation scope or any evaluation function.

On simpler terms, it prevents the creation of any policy definition which will evaluate nothing.

This feature is enabled by default in the distributed tractusx-edc helm charts. In order to disable the feature or if you don't use the distributed helm chart, and you want to enable this feature, it can be toggled via configuration or environment variable using the following config:

edc.policy.validation.enabled=true|false

docs.title: 2. Removal of Azure based distributions
docs.text:
As they were previously marked for deprecation, the azure vault based distributions were effectively removed and WILL NOT be distributed any longer. Be aware this has nothing to do with the cloud related extensions we support, such as Azure blob or AWS S3 provisioners and dataplanes. Those are still included as part of the base tractusx-edc distribution.ß

If you installation relied on any tractusx-edc azure-vault distribution (either docker image or helm chart), please also be aware that you will no longer find a distribution for this or future releases.

docs.title: 3. Updated and Deprecated BPNL Group operators
docs.text:
Special attention is necessary towards policy definitions that contain BPNL group constrains using either the eq or neq operators. These have been deprecated in favor of the isAllOf, isAnyOf and isNoneOf operators which are the proper operators for sets.

Additionally, the behavior of the isAllOf operator has been fixed since it previously failed validation for BPNLs that were assigned to 3 distinct groups, 2 of which were the same as listed in the policy constrain. The isAllOf now checks if a certain BPNL is assigned to all the groups allowed in the policy definition.

The IN operator was also fixed, since it evaluated the same as the faulty isAllOf operator. It now performs the same as the isAnyOf operator.

docs.title: 4. Store Migrations
docs.text:
For connector operators who maintain specific flyway migration files, please be aware of new migrations added in these PRs:

  • https://github.com/eclipse-tractusx/tractusx-edc/pull/1706
  • https://github.com/eclipse-tractusx/tractusx-edc/pull/1713

docs.title: Migration Guide 0.9.x -> 0.10.x
docs.text:
This document outlines the necessary changes for migrating your tractusx-edc installation from versions 0.9.x to 0.10.0. It also outlines some points that adopters and operators should pay close attention to when migrating from one version to another.

This document is not a comprehensive feature list.

  • Migration Guide 0.9.x -> 0.10.x
  • 1. DCP version 0.8 setting

docs.title: 1. DCP version 0.8 setting
docs.text:
In the upstream EDC the development of the DCP v1.0 made the v0.8 sort of legacy, and it needs explicit configuration. So this setting is required to permit correct interaction with the DIM:

edc.dcp.v08.forced=true

docs.title: Migration Guide 0.10.x -> 0.11.x
docs.text:
This document outlines the necessary changes for migrating your tractusx-edc installation from versions 0.10.x to 0.11.0. It also outlines some points that adopters and operators should pay close attention to when migrating from one version to another.

This document is not a comprehensive feature list.

  • Migration Guide 0.10.x -> 0.11.x
  • 1. DCP version 1.0
  • 2. Participant ID
  • 3. Protocol handling for different versions
  • 4. Policy validations and general policy handling according to standard CX-0152
    • Impact on migration

docs.title: 1. DCP version 1.0
docs.text: Tractus-X EDC now uses DCP 1.0 by default — no switch is required. If DCP 0.8.1 was previously forced via edc.dcp.v08.forced, that setting should be removed; it is deprecated and no flag is provided for 1.0.

docs.title: 2. Participant ID
docs.text:
Previously, the BPN was used as the EDC's participant identifier. Starting with 0.11.0, the primary participant identifier is now the DID. As the BPN is still required for some processes and also will be used for communication with older Tractus-X EDC versions, it now needs to be supplied via a new setting. Therefore, the configuration should be updated as follows:

edc.participant.id=<did>
tractusx.edc.participant.bpn=<bpn>

docs.title: 3. Protocol handling for different versions
docs.text:
The 0.11.0 Tractus-X EDC supports both the previously supported 0.8 version of DSP as well as the new 2025-1 version of DSP. It is in the responsibility of the caller of a management api call to identify the version to be used. The relevant properties are counterPartyAddress, as the EDC supports different versions as own subtrees in the rest api hierarchy, protocol and counterPartyId, resp. policy/assigner. For a standard runtime, the parameters have to be set:

Properties to be used for version 0.8:

counterPartyAddress=https://<provider-connector-url>/api/v1/dsp
protocol=dataspace-protocol-http
counterPartyId, resp. policy/assigner=<provider-bpn>

For version 2025-1:

counterPartyAddress=https://<provider-connector-url>/api/v1/dsp/2025-1
protocol=dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1
counterPartyId, resp. policy/assigner=<provider-did>

The property values to be used for a specific connector can be retrieved from the new management endpoint /v4alpha/connectordiscovery/dspversionparams. It takes as request parameter a payload like:

{
  "@context": {
    "tx": "https://w3id.org/tractusx/v0.0.1/ns/",
    "edc": "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/"
  },
  "tx:bpnl": "BPNL1234567890",
  "edc:counterPartyAddress": "https://provider.domain.com/api/v1/dsp"
}

As response, it returns all the right version parameter for that connector, depending on whether it supports DSP 2025-1 or only the old protocol 0.8. For the above example, it would return for version 0.8:

{
  "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/counterPartyAddress": "https://provider.domain.com/api/v1/dsp/",
  "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/counterPartyId": "BPNL1234567890",
  "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/protocol": "dataspace-protocol-http"
}

and for version 2025-1:

{
  "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/counterPartyAddress": "https://provider.domain.com/api/v1/dsp/2025-1",
  "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/counterPartyId": "<provider-did>",
  "https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/protocol": "dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1"
}

docs.title: 4. Policy validations and general policy handling according to standard CX-0152
docs.text:
Standard CX-0152 specifies a set of standardized contract building blocks that can be used within policies to express the usage conditions for a data transfer as well as the access filters used by a provider to select data offers for a catalog request. The new connector version 0.11.0 provides validation of the correct usage of these building blocks during creation of a policy. Policies are now validated in their entirety including action types, rule types, constraint logic, left and right operand values, as well as operators.

The introduction of the new standard CX-0152 comes with another consequence. As the formal specification of the building blocks have been improved, all existing left operands have been moved to a different JSON-LD namespace. The consequence is that a policy which is valid in a Jupiter dataspace has to be adapted to be usable in a Saturn dataspace. It was the decision of the Catena-X standardization body, that it is acceptable for all data provider to duplicate contract definitions, having one contract definition targeted to consumer acting on Jupiter level and one contract definition targeted at consumer acting on Saturn level. Each contract definition has a usage policy with building blocks defined either for a Jupiter consumer or a Saturn consumer. This way, backward compatibility is ensured, as a provider can do data transfer offers for both ecosystem versions.

The handling of the different policies has been connected to the DSP version used for the interaction. Due to the introduction of DSP version 2025-1 as mandatory DSP version used on Saturn level, usage policies fulfilling the Jupiter standard are handled by the DSP version 0.8 support within the connector, whereas usage policies fulfilling the Saturn standard are handled by the DSP version 2025-1 support.

A consequence of this is that a consumer sees both offers and has to decide based on his own capabilities (Jupiter or Saturn), which offer to negotiate for. The difference can be determined by the namespace used for defining the operands. A policy fulfilling the Saturn standard CX-0152 will have a context binding like this:

{
  ...,
  "@context": [
    "https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/context.jsonld",
    ...,
  ],
  ...
}

Another impact on the new policies affects access policies, i.e., the policies in a contract definition that are used to filter catalog entries. Access policies are not in the scope of backward compatibility, i.e., an access policy never leaves the provider connector. As a consequence, in a connector of version 0.11.0, only policies according to CX-0152 on Saturn level are usable, old access policies are not evaluated correctly, i.e., a contract definition that uses such a policy will never be visible in a catalog. Be aware, that it is still possible to create Jupiter-level policies and to use them as access policies, as the contract definition creation does not block that.

docs.title: Impact on migration
docs.text:
For someone updating a connector from a version 0.10.0 or earlier to 0.11.0, the mentioned aspects have the following consequences:

  • A migration in principle is possible, the database will be updated to support the new connector version and all table content will be kept as is.
  • The existing usage policies can be used for contract definitions targeted at Jupiter consumers.
  • The existing access policies become obsolete, as the general semantic has not changed, a simple conversion of the existing policies can be done. The basic change is the new namespace that is needed for the building blocks used in the policy. As a consequence a requested catalog will not contain any contract offer that makes use of an old access policy after the upgrade to 0.11.
  • The existing contract definitions need to be adapted to a new access policy. These adapted contract definition will then fulfill the purpose of defining data offers for Jupiter consumers.
  • The existing contract definitions should be copied and redefined with a new usage policy to make data offers for Saturn consumers.
  • The migration and duplication of offers can of course be influenced by knowledge you have about potential consumers, e.g., if you have contract definitions for very dedicated consumers, and you know their update strategy, concerning Saturn, you can postpone the creation of new contract definitions until needed by that customer and can delete existing definition as soon as the consumer has switched.

For more information on the CX-0152 standard, please refer to the official specification. The following link to the standard might break soon enough, when CX-0152 becomes active in the Saturn ecosystem release, remove the next path part in that case. - Catena-X Dataspace Policy Standard (CX-0152)

There is an extensive documentation on contracting in Catena-X in the regulatory framework: - Catena-X Regulatory Framework - Contracting

A recommended playground to experiment with the new policies is the Tractus-X Policy Builder which can be found here: - Catena-X Policy Builder

docs.title: Removal of "dcat:endpointUrl" in catalog response
docs.text: Until EDC 0.10 there were two attributes "dcat:endpointUrl" and "dcat:endpointURL" present in the catalog response. The first one presented an inconsistency with the dataspace protocol specification and thus was removed with the 0.11 release. Applications that use "dcat:endpointUrl" need to switch to "dcat:endpointURL".

docs.title: Migration Guide 0.11.x -> 0.12.x
docs.text:
This document outlines the necessary changes for migrating your tractusx-edc installation from versions 0.11.x to 0.12.x. It also outlines some points that adopters and operators should pay close attention to when migrating from one version to another.

This document is not a comprehensive feature list.

  • Migration Guide 0.11.x -> 0.12.x
  • 1. Connector Discovery
    • Self-Registration of Connectors in DID Document
    • Discovery of Connectors
    • Changed Param Discovery Request Body
  • 2. Participant ID
  • 3. Changed behavior for old policies
  • 4. Verifiable Presentation Caching
  • 5. Catalog response changes
  • 6. Deprecation of https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/odrl.jsonld context
  • 7. Deprecated instances

docs.title: Self-Registration of Connectors in DID Document
docs.text:
The connector provides a new feature that automatically registers a running connectors in the DID documents service section, so that it is published to be discovered by potential consumers. The feature is can be enabled. The following three parameters allow you to influence the execution of this feature.

TX_EDC_DID_SERVICE_SELF_REGISTRATION_ENABLED=true
TX_EDC_DID_SERVICE_SELF_DEREGISTRATION_ENABLED=false
TX_EDC_DID_SERVICE_SELF_REGISTRATION_ID="did:web:connector_id"

The registration enabled parameter turns on self registration on startup. For a standard one instance connector setup, it is recommended to also enable the deregistration enabled parameter, as this automatically deregisters the connector during shutdown. This allows a full controlled life-cycle of the availability of the connector in the decentral discovery. For setups with a scaling connector or other scenarios, where the availability of a connector is not bound on it, currently executed, this auto deregistration leads to issues, that is, why it can the deregistration can be disabled explicitly.

The third parameter is a requirement from the format given for service entries in a DID document. Such a record requires a unique id for the connector, which is typically in the did format. The content actually is only used as a string, so the concrete content has no further constraints bound to it.

Be aware, that in the standard helm charts, only the first and third parameter can be set in the values file:

iatp:
  didService:
    selfRegistration:
      # -- Whether Service Self Registration is enabled
      enabled: false
      # -- Unique id of connector to be used for register / unregister service inside did document (must be valid URI)
      id: "did:web:changeme"

The value for the second parameter is determined from other parameters like the scaling setting for the deployment. If an adopter wants to influence the deregistration procedure explicitly, he has to adapt the template setting for that parameter.

docs.title: Discovery of Connectors
docs.text:
There is a new endpoint in the management api /v4alpha/connectordiscovery/connectors that supports the decentral discovery of DSP endpoints. The api takes a did as parameter edc:counterPartyId and does the did based connector endpoint retrieval according to the DSP spec. I.e., it downloads the DID document, searches for service entries of type DataService. For each found endpoint, the version metadata endpoint is called to determine the dsp versions supported by the connector and the appropriate one is selected. For each connector the right connection parameters are extracted and returned as an array of connection parameters.

For the time being the parameter given to the endpoint can also be a BPNL, but it is strictly recommended to start with the DID. The BPNL mechanism is only provided as legacy mechanism as long as central Catena-X mechanisms do not properly allow to search for the DID of the counterparty.

For a proper discovery of connectors operated by a business partner, this method is strongly recommended to be used in a proper discover, retrieve catalog, initiate data transfer cycle!

docs.title: Changed Param Discovery Request Body
docs.text: The already existing management api endpoint /v4alpha/connectordiscovery/dspversionparams, introduced in version 0.11.0 has been adapted to be more neutral. For that reason, the endpoints payload now requires the two parameters counterPartyAddress and counterPartyId. The latter has been renamed from the parameter name bpnl. It is recommended to switch the parameter name in addressing the endpoint, for backward compatibility reasons, the parameter bpnl still works but is a candidate to be removed in a later version.

docs.title: 2. Participant ID
docs.text:
In preparation of the new multi-tenancy ability of the connector, a participant context id has been introduced, that represents the future tenant id. The new identifier is mandatory and has been added to the helm charts:

participant:
  # -- BPN Number
  id: "BPNLCHANGEME"
  # -- Participant Context Id - Newly introduced id for a connector instance (needed for multitenancy)
  contextId: "UUID CHANGEME"
The actual setting/environment variable for the connector is named EDC_PARTICIPANT_CONTEXT_ID.

The participant context id is recommended to be a uuid. A minimum requirement is, that it can be used within a url path as segment to make it usable for a tenant id later on.

Note, that the connector contains a code segment that prevents starting a connector, if the identifier is not set.

docs.title: 3. Changed behavior for old policies
docs.text:
There is a change when old policies are compacted in a response from the management api. The behavior in 0.12.0 is breaking in contrast to Jupiter versions 0.10.x and earlier. The issue is, that with the redefinition of the policies, the prefix json-ld cx-policy has been redefined for the new policies.

When creating an old policy at the management api, nothing changes, as you control the json-ld namespace, i.e., by using

{
  "@context": {
    "cx-policy": "https://w3id.org/catenax/policy/"
  }
}

You still can refer to old policy terms in this way cx-policy:UsagePurpose. The issue is, that in the other direction, when requesting a policy via the management api, the connector cannot compact anymore to cx-policy:Usage-Purpose because in that direction, due to a breaking change in the Catena-X standardization, the prefix cx-policy is bound to https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/.

Due to a bug in 0.11.0 json-ld compacting is not done for Catena-X specifics in the management api, so 0.11.0 already has breaking behavior in comparison with 0.10.x and earlier. In 0.12.0, we fix these deviations, but for old policies, based on the https://w3id.org/catenax/policy/ namespace, we cannot provide a solution, i.e., these terms in responses from the management api will always be fully expanded. This is the only solution, that does not add a breaking change on the level of json-ld, but a pure json based handling of responses will see unavoidable differences.

docs.title: 4. Verifiable Presentation Caching
docs.text:
A new feature in the connector allows to cache verifiable presentations requested from the wallet to reduce the amount of requests to the consumer wallet and to improve processing time. The feature as such is switchable, using the boolean configuration parameter TX_EDC_DCP_CACHE_ENABLED. By default, it is enabled. A second parameter TX_EDC_DCP_CACHE_VALIDITY_SECONDS allows for an enabled cache to define the length of the validity of a cache entry in seconds. This defaults to 24h, as the development group rated the delayed recognition of a revoked credential as acceptable. The settings can be changed with the mentioned parameters/environment variables. For the helm charts there is a new section in the values file that allows the setting of the parameters.

iatp:
  cache:
    # -- Whether the Verifiable Presentation cache is enabled
    enabled: true
    # -- Validity of the Verifiable Presentation cache in seconds
    validity: 86400

docs.title: 5. Catalog response changes
docs.text: Starting with version 0.11.0, the catalog response returned by /v3/catalog/request was changed (see walkthrough). Each distribution entry now exposes its format as a simple string (for example AzureStorage-PUSH, HttpData-PULL, AmazonS3-PUSH), and the top-level service attribute is an array of DataService objects instead of a single object. This representation is emitted for DSP2025-1 catalogs and should be expected by clients. The legacy structure is still emitted only when interacting with DSP0.8 connectors for backward compatibility.

docs.title: 6. Deprecation of https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/odrl.jsonld context
docs.text:
The Catena-X Data Sovereignty Expert Group has decommissioned the 'odrl' context named https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/odrl.jsonld as this was a redundant copy of the original dataspace subset of ODRL as defined in the context https://w3id.org/dspace/2025/1/odrl-profile.jsonld. The current version still handles the obsolete context properly, when seen as input, but JSON-LD compacting will not consider the old context.

Note: This does not affect the https://w3id.org/catenax/2025/9/policy/context.jsonld context which defines the policy constraints of the Catena-X policy framework, it only affects the specification of the ODRL defined elements usable for expressing policies.

docs.title: 7. Deprecated instances
docs.text:
The Data Plane Selector Configuration Extension has been removed, as it has been deprecated since version 0.7.2. Additionally, several configuration parameters deprecated since version 0.7.x have also been removed. Please use the updated configuration parameters instead.

VaultSeedExtension:

Old value New value New environment variable edc.vault.secrets tx.edc.vault.secrets TX_EDC_VAULT_SECRETS

BdrsClientExtension:

Old value New value New environment variable tx.iam.iatp.bdrs.server.url tx.edc.iam.iatp.bdrs.server.url TX_EDC_IAM_IATP_BDRS_SERVER_URL tx.iam.iatp.credentialservice.url tx.edc.iam.iatp.credentialservice.url TX_EDC_IAM_IATP_CREDENTIALSERVICE_URL tx.iam.iatp.bdrs.cache.validity tx.edc.iam.iatp.bdrs.cache.validity TX_EDC_IAM_IATP_BDRS_CACHE_VALIDITY

DataPlaneProxyConsumerApiExtension:

Old value New value New environment variable tx.dpf.consumer.proxy.port tx.edc.dpf.consumer.proxy.port TX_EDC_DPF_CONSUMER_PROXY_PORT tx.dpf.consumer.proxy.thread.pool tx.edc.dpf.consumer.proxy.thread.pool TX_EDC_DPF_CONSUMER_PROXY_THREAD_POOL edc.api.auth.key.alias tx.edc.dpf.consumer.proxy.auth.apikey.alias TX_EDC_DPF_CONSUMER_PROXY_AUTH_APIKEY_ALIAS edc.api.auth.key tx.edc.dpf.consumer.proxy.auth.apikey TX_EDC_DPF_CONSUMER_PROXY_AUTH_APIKEY

DataPlaneTokenRefreshServiceExtension:

Old value New value New environment variable edc.dataplane.token.expiry.tolerance tx.edc.dataplane.token.expiry.tolerance TX_EDC_DATAPLANE_TOKEN_EXPIRY_TOLERANCE edc.dataplane.token.refresh.endpoint tx.edc.dataplane.token.refresh.endpoint TX_EDC_DATAPLANE_TOKEN_REFRESH_ENDPOINT edc.dataplane.token.expiry tx.edc.dataplane.token.expiry TX_EDC_DATAPLANE_TOKEN_EXPIRY

RemoteTokenServiceClientExtension:

Old value New value New environment variable edc.iam.sts.dim.url tx.edc.iam.sts.dim.url TX_EDC_IAM_STS_DIM_URL

AbstractPostgresqlMigrationExtension:

Old value New value New environment variable org.eclipse.tractusx.edc.postgresql.migration.<subsystem>.enabled tx.edc.postgresql.migration.<subsystem>.enabled TX_EDC_POSTGRESQL_MIGRATION_<SUBSYSTEM>_ENABLED org.eclipse.tractusx.edc.postgresql.migration.schema tx.edc.postgresql.migration.schema TX_EDC_POSTGRESQL_MIGRATION_SCHEMA

docs.title: Migration Guide 0.12.x -> 0.13.x
docs.text:
This document outlines the necessary changes for migrating your tractusx-edc installation from versions 0.12.x to 0.13.x. It also outlines some points that adopters and operators should pay close attention to when migrating from one version to another.

This document is not a comprehensive feature list.

  • Migration Guide 0.12.x -> 0.13.x
  • 1. Federate Catalog removal
  • 2. Deprecated instances
  • 3. Postgres Version
  • 4. Participant identity configuration
  • 5. IATP renamed to DCP
  • 6. DIM renamed to DIV
  • 7. DID document service self-registration
  • 8. New optional Kafka data flow extension

docs.title: 1. Federate Catalog removal
docs.text:
The Federate Catalog feature has not been proven to be usable, that's why it will be removed. The deletion of the table edc_federated_catalog will be done automatically by migration script. If you need to keep the data, please make sure that tx.edc.postgresql.migration.federatedcatalog.enabled is set to false before the migration.

Along with the feature, the Helm values controlplane.catalog.* and controlplane.endpoints.catalog.* and the corresponding EDC_CATALOG_CACHE_*, TX_EDC_CATALOG_NODE_LIST_FILE and WEB_HTTP_CATALOG_* settings have been removed and must be deleted from your configuration.

docs.title: 2. Deprecated instances
docs.text:
API changes:

Old API New API /business-partner-groups /v3/business-partner-groups /v2/edrs /v3/edrs /v4alpha/connectordiscovery /v3/connectordiscovery /v4alpha/dataflows /v3/dataflows

The endpoints previously available under v4alpha have been provided under management API v3 as well. The v4alpha variants are still served, but are marked as deprecated since 0.13.0. Switching to the v3 paths is therefore not required for this upgrade, but it is recommended, as the v4alpha variants will be removed in a future release.

Additionally, several configuration parameters deprecated since version 0.8.x have also been removed. Please use the updated configuration parameters instead.

SqlBusinessPartnerGroupStoreExtension:

Old value New value New environment variable edc.datasource.bpn.name edc.sql.store.bpn.datasource EDC_SQL_STORE_BPN_DATASOURCE

SqlEdrLockExtension:

Old value New value New environment variable edc.datasource.edr.name edc.sql.store.edr.datasource EDC_SQL_STORE_EDR_DATASOURCE

2026_06-Version_0.12.x_0.13.x.md

docs.title: 3. Postgres Version
docs.text:
The new version provides Postgres version 18.0 as dependency in the helm charts referring to the Cloud Pirates helm charts and the official Postgres docker image instead of the formerly used bitnami charts and docker images.

As a consequence, for a Kubernetes setup done with the provided helm charts, there is no possibility to do an automatic upgrade with the provided helm charts, as the two images are not supporting that. Instead, during update, an operator has to follow the general migration guide

Further, the chart now differentiates between admin and custom user. It is recommended to use a custom user. Please follow the database configuration section of the helm documentation of the tractusx-connector.

docs.title: 4. Participant identity configuration
docs.text:
The meaning of the Helm value participant.id has changed. It now carries the DID of the connector (the value that was previously configured under iatp.id), while the BPNL moved to the new value participant.bpnl.

Old Helm value New Helm value Content iatp.id participant.id DID, e.g. did:web:changeme participant.id participant.bpnl BPNL, e.g. BPNL0000000000XX

This maps to the runtime configuration as follows:

Environment variable Setting Content EDC_PARTICIPANT_ID edc.participant.id DID of the connector EDC_IAM_ISSUER_ID edc.iam.issuer.id DID of the connector TRACTUSX_EDC_PARTICIPANT_BPN tractusx.edc.participant.bpn BPNL of the connector EDC_PARTICIPANT_CONTEXT_ID edc.participant.context.id Participant context id (UUID)

[!IMPORTANT] edc.participant.context.id remains a mandatory setting and must never change once set. It is now also used to derive the DID document service id, see section 7.

docs.title: 5. IATP renamed to DCP
docs.text:
The former "IATP" naming has been consistently replaced by "DCP" (Decentralized Claims Protocol). This affects the Helm values, the runtime settings and the module coordinates.

Helm values: the whole iatp block has been renamed to dcp (iatp.trustedIssuers -> dcp.trustedIssuers, iatp.cache.* -> dcp.cache.*, iatp.didService.* -> dcp.didService.*, iatp.sts.* -> dcp.sts.*).

Runtime settings:

Old setting New setting New environment variable tx.edc.iam.iatp.bdrs.server.url tx.edc.iam.dcp.bdrs.server.url TX_EDC_IAM_DCP_BDRS_SERVER_URL tx.edc.iam.iatp.bdrs.cache.validity tx.edc.iam.dcp.bdrs.cache.validity TX_EDC_IAM_DCP_BDRS_CACHE_VALIDITY tx.edc.iam.iatp.credentialservice.url tx.edc.iam.dcp.credentialservice.url TX_EDC_IAM_DCP_CREDENTIALSERVICE_URL tx.edc.iam.iatp.default-scopes.* tx.edc.iam.dcp.default-scopes.* TX_EDC_IAM_DCP_DEFAULT_SCOPES_*

Module coordinates (only relevant for adopters assembling their own runtimes): the tx-dcp extension has been split into edc-extensions:dcp:tx-dcp (protocol-agnostic parts) and edc-extensions:dcp:cx-dcp (Catena-X specific default scopes and scope extractors). Both are part of edc-controlplane-base, so operators using the published images or Helm charts are not affected. Java packages were renamed from org.eclipse.tractusx.edc.iam.iatp to org.eclipse.tractusx.edc.iam.dcp accordingly.

docs.title: 6. DIM renamed to DIV
docs.text:
The Decentralized Identity Management (DIM) naming has been replaced by Decentralized Identity Verification (DIV).

Helm values:

Old Helm value New Helm value iatp.sts.dim.url dcp.sts.div.url iatp.sts.oauth.token_url dcp.sts.oauth.token_url iatp.sts.oauth.client.id dcp.sts.oauth.client.id iatp.sts.oauth.client.secret_alias dcp.sts.oauth.client.secret_alias

Runtime settings:

Old setting New setting New environment variable tx.edc.iam.sts.dim.url tx.edc.iam.sts.div.url TX_EDC_IAM_STS_DIV_URL

The corresponding modules were renamed as well: edc-extensions:dcp:tx-dcp-sts-dim -> edc-extensions:dcp:tx-dcp-sts-div and edc-extensions:did-document:did-document-service-dim -> edc-extensions:did-document:did-document-service-div.

docs.title: 7. DID document service self-registration
docs.text:
The setting tx.edc.did.service.self.registration.id (Helm value iatp.didService.selfRegistration.id, environment variable TX_EDC_DID_SERVICE_SELF_REGISTRATION_ID) has been removed. The service id used for registering / unregistering the connector's data service entry in the DID document is now derived from the participant context id as urn:<edc.participant.context.id>.

[!WARNING] If self-registration was enabled in 0.12.x with an explicitly configured id, the previously registered service entry will no longer be found under the new id. Remove the stale entry from the DID document manually (or unregister it before upgrading) to avoid a duplicated data service entry.

tx.edc.did.service.self.registration.enabled and tx.edc.did.service.self.deregistration.enabled (Helm: dcp.didService.selfRegistration.enabled) are unchanged.

docs.title: 8. New optional Kafka data flow extension
docs.text:
A Kafka broker extension with OAuth2 integration for data flows has been added (edc-extensions:dataplane:kafka:kafka-broker-extension, data-address-kafka, validator-data-address-kafka). It is not part of the published data plane images and has to be added explicitly to a custom runtime. When enabled, it supports broker-level access revocation via Kafka ACLs, configured through:

Setting Default Description edc.dataplane.kafka.acl.enabled false Enable Kafka ACL management for immediate broker-level revocation edc.dataplane.kafka.acl.bootstrap.servers - Bootstrap servers of the ACL admin client (required when ACL enabled) edc.dataplane.kafka.acl.security.protocol PLAINTEXT Security protocol of the ACL admin client edc.dataplane.kafka.acl.sasl.mechanism - SASL mechanism of the ACL admin client (e.g. OAUTHBEARER, PLAIN) edc.dataplane.kafka.acl.sasl.jaas.config - SASL JAAS config of the ACL admin client

See the extension README for details.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Running a connector day to day: knowing that it is healthy, finding out why something failed, and fixing it.

  • Observability

    Health checks, logs, OpenTelemetry and business events.

    Observe

  • Tune for production

    Log level, JVM memory, replicas, state machines, database pool, caches and timeouts.

    Tune

  • Troubleshooting

    Common symptoms, their causes and the fix.

    Diagnose

  • Production checklist

    The hardening steps before you go live.

    Harden

  • Upgrades

    Release model, support policy and the upgrade procedure.

    Upgrade

docs.title: A healthy connector at a glance
docs.text:
kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=<release>      # all Running and READY
helm test <release>                                           # chart test passes
kubectl logs deploy/<release>-controlplane | grep -i "ready"  # runtime finished booting

And from the outside: your partners can request your catalog, and your own catalog requests to them succeed.

docs.title: Health checks
docs.text:
Each runtime exposes liveness and readiness on its default API context (port 8080 in the chart):

Probe URL Liveness GET http://<pod>:8080/api/check/liveness Readiness GET http://<pod>:8080/api/check/readiness

The chart configures both as Kubernetes probes (initial delay 30 s, period 10 s, timeout 5 s, failure threshold 6). Tune them under controlplane.livenessProbe / readinessProbe and the dataplane.* equivalents.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
The runtimes log through Log4j 2. By default the chart writes JSON logs to stdout, ready for Loki, Elasticsearch or any other log pipeline.

Helm value Default Meaning log4j2.enableJsonLogs true Use the JSON layout from log4j2.config (mounted as /app/log4j2.yaml) log4j2.config JSON template layout Full Log4j 2 YAML configuration, if you want your own controlplane.logs.level, dataplane.logs.level DEBUG Log level passed as --log-level

Use INFO in production

DEBUG is verbose and can make it hard to find what matters. Switch to INFO and raise the level temporarily when you investigate a problem.

What to search for:

You want to know… Look for Whether the runtime started the line announcing that the runtime is ready, after all extensions were started Why a catalog or negotiation was rejected Policy, evaluation, credential, VerifiablePresentation Database migration problems Flyway, migration Token refresh problems refresh, token

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
The image ships the OpenTelemetry Java agent. It is off by default. Enable and configure it through the properties file the chart mounts as /app/opentelemetry.properties:

controlplane:
  opentelemetry: |-
    otel.javaagent.enabled=true
    otel.service.name=my-connector-controlplane
    otel.exporter.otlp.endpoint=http://otel-collector:4318

The same exists under dataplane.opentelemetry. All otel.* keys follow the agent configuration.

docs.title: Business events
docs.text:
The event-subscriber extension sends connector events (negotiation, transfer, …) as OpenTelemetry log records to a collector, which gives you an audit trail of data exchanges.

Setting Default Meaning tx.edc.otel.events.subscriber.active false Turn the subscriber on tx.edc.otel.events.endpoint http://localhost:4318/v1/logs OTLP/HTTP logs endpoint tx.edc.otel.service.name unknown_service service.name of the records

Set them with controlplane.env / dataplane.env, for example TX_EDC_OTEL_EVENTS_SUBSCRIBER_ACTIVE: "true".

Your applications can also be notified directly: register callbackAddresses on negotiations and transfers, or configure static callbacks. See the EDR walkthrough.

docs.title: Useful Management API queries
docs.text:
Q='{"@context":{"@vocab":"https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/"},"@type":"QuerySpec","limit":100}'

# Negotiations that ended badly, with the reason
curl -s -X POST "$MGMT/v3/contractnegotiations/request" -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$Q" | jq '.[] | select(.state=="TERMINATED") | {"@id", counterPartyId, errorDetail}'

# Running transfers
curl -s -X POST "$MGMT/v3/transferprocesses/request" -H "X-Api-Key: $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$Q" | jq '.[] | select(.state=="STARTED") | {"@id", assetId, contractId}'

A terminated negotiation or transfer carries an errorDetail field that explains why.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Find your symptom, check the likely causes in order, apply the fix. If you are stuck, open a discussion with the log lines and your (redacted) values.

flowchart TD
  s{Where does it fail?}
  s --> boot[Runtime does not start]
  s --> api[Management API call fails]
  s --> cat[Catalog empty or failing]
  s --> neg[Negotiation TERMINATED]
  s --> data[Transfer or data access fails]
  s --> k8s[Kubernetes deployment]

docs.title: The runtime does not start
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Fix The participant context id has not been set, it is a mandatory setting now edc.participant.context.id is missing; the database migration needs it Set participant.contextId in the chart (env EDC_PARTICIPANT_CONTEXT_ID). Never change it afterwards. Flyway error, or column … does not exist Migrations disabled, or the database is ahead of or behind the image Keep tx.edc.postgresql.migration.enabled=true; check the flyway_schema_history table; read the migration guide of the version you came from. Missing-setting error at boot A required setting has no value The message names the key. Look it up with the setting-lifecycle skill or in Configuration. Vault errors on every secret HashiCorp Vault 1.18.1, wrong token or wrong paths.secret Use a different Vault version; check vault.hashicorp.url, the token and vault.hashicorp.paths.secret (default /v1/secret). Pod restarts after ~90 s Liveness probe fails while the runtime is still booting or the database is slow Look at the log for the real error first; increase livenessProbe.initialDelaySeconds if boot is just slow.

docs.title: Management API calls fail
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Fix 401 Unauthorized Wrong or missing X-Api-Key, or delegated auth is configured Use the value of controlplane.endpoints.management.authKey. With jwksUrl set, send a JWT instead. 404 on a path that should exist Wrong base path or port Management is :8081/management in the chart, so paths look like /management/v3/assets. 400 when creating a policy Catena-X policy validation rejected it The response lists the failing constraint. Compare with Catena-X policies: action access vs use, operator, right operand type (array for isAnyOf). 400 when creating a contract definition Access policy must have action access and contract policy action use; or an empty asset selector is blocked Fix the referenced policies. The empty-selector blocker is controlled by tx.edc.validator.contractdefinitions.block-empty-asset-selector (default false). 400 with a JSON-LD message A term does not expand to the IRI you expect Check the @context; with @vocab every unknown term becomes an EDC term.

docs.title: The catalog is empty or the request fails
docs.text:
Work through the identity chain, consumer first, then provider:

  1. Consumer can get a token. Its STS / DIV settings (dcp.sts.*) are correct and the client secret exists in Vault under dcp.sts.oauth.client.secret_alias.
  2. Consumer has the credentials. A MembershipCredential (and for DSP 2025-1 also DataExchangeGovernanceCredential and BpnCredential) exists in its wallet and is not expired or revoked.
  3. Provider trusts the issuer. The issuer's DID is in the provider's dcp.trustedIssuers.
  4. Provider can resolve the BPN. controlplane.bdrs.server.url points to a reachable BDRS.
  5. Addresses and protocol match. counterPartyAddress ends with /api/v1/dsp/2025-1 for dataspace-protocol-http:2025-1, and counterPartyId is the provider's DID (BPNL for DSP 0.8). Use connector discovery when unsure.
  6. The access policy admits you. If everything else works but one dataset is missing, its access policy (for example a BusinessPartnerGroup) excludes you.

The detailed identity flow is in Identity and trust.

docs.title: A negotiation ends in TERMINATED
docs.text: Cause Fix The offer in your request is not identical to the one in the catalog Copy the policy from odrl:hasPolicy unchanged; add only assigner and target. You do not satisfy the contract policy Check credentials for FrameworkAgreement / Membership; read errorDetail of the negotiation. Wrong assigner Use the provider's DID (DSP 2025-1) or BPNL (DSP 0.8).

docs.title: Transfers and data access
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Fix Transfer TERMINATED right after the request Agreement retired or expired, or the transfer-time policy fails Check /v3/contractagreements/retirements/request on the provider and the errorDetail of the transfer. 401 from the provider data plane Token expired Fetch the EDR with auto_refresh=true, or use the consumer proxy. Refresh returns 401 repeatedly Consumer lost the rotated refresh token (older versions), or the refresh request is not authenticated with the consumer's identity Upgrade; current versions accept the previous refresh token until the new one is used. Restart the transfer as a last resort. Consumer proxy unreachable after changing its port The port is configured in two places When you change dataplane.endpoints.proxy.port, also set TX_EDC_DPF_CONSUMER_PROXY_PORT. Upload or multipart request fails with a file system error readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and the temp directory is not writable Make sure temporary files go to the writable /tmp volume; as a last resort relax the security context. Provider data plane cannot reach the backend baseUrl not reachable from the data plane pod, or backend credentials missing in Vault Test from the pod; check the secret alias in the asset's dataAddress.

docs.title: Kubernetes deployment
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Fix no matches for kind "HorizontalPodAutoscaler" in version "autoscaling/v2beta1" The chart's HPA templates use an API that current Kubernetes no longer serves Keep autoscaling.enabled: false and scale with replicaCount, or provide your own HPA. helm install fails with a required error A mandatory value is empty Set it, or a non-empty placeholder if the real value comes from a Secret (see Configuration). Data lost after a pod restart Bundled PostgreSQL without persistence or Vault in dev mode Use external PostgreSQL and Vault (production checklist). Partners get http:// URLs TLS not enabled on the first ingress Set tls.enabled: true on the protocol/public ingress; the chart then advertises https://.

docs.title: Ask the Sensei
docs.text: The Connector Sensei can read your logs and settings against the code at your exact version, and point to the line that rejects your request.

docs.title: Tune for production
docs.text:
The chart defaults are made to start anywhere, not to carry production load. This page lists the knobs that matter once the connector runs for real, in the order you will usually need them. Change one thing at a time and watch the effect in your metrics and logs.

Before you tune, work through the production checklist: it covers security and availability; this page covers performance and resource use.

docs.title: Settings in the Helm chart
docs.text:
Every EDC setting below can be set as an environment variable through controlplane.env or dataplane.env: write the key in upper case with _ instead of . and - (edc.transfer.state-machine.batch-size becomes EDC_TRANSFER_STATE_MACHINE_BATCH_SIZE). See Configuration.

values.yaml (excerpt)
controlplane:
  logs:
    level: INFO
  resources:
    requests: { cpu: "1", memory: 2Gi }
    limits: { cpu: "2", memory: 2Gi }
  env:
    JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0"
    EDC_TRANSFER_STATE_MACHINE_BATCH_SIZE: "50"

docs.title: 1. Log level
docs.text: The chart sets the log level of both planes to DEBUG (controlplane.logs.level, dataplane.logs.level). In production that is a lot of output, and it may contain request details. Set INFO, and switch to DEBUG only while you investigate a problem.

docs.title: 2. Memory and the JVM
docs.text:
Value Chart default *.resources.requests.memory / *.resources.limits.memory 1024Mi / 1024Mi *.resources.requests.cpu / *.resources.limits.cpu 500m / 1.5

The images run Java 25 (Eclipse Temurin). Inside a container the JVM uses 25 % of the memory limit as maximum heap by default, so a 1 GiB pod gets about 256 MiB of heap. Give the heap more of the pod with JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0 in *.env, and keep the memory request equal to the limit, so the pod is not evicted under node pressure.

debug.enabled uses JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS too

With controlplane.debug.enabled or dataplane.debug.enabled, the chart sets JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS itself for the remote debugger. Do not set it in env at the same time; debugging is not for production anyway.

Signs that memory is too small: restarts with OOMKilled, long garbage collection pauses in the JVM metrics, or timeouts under load. CPU limits mainly slow down the start (class loading, JIT); readiness probes start after 30 seconds by default.

docs.title: 3. Replicas
docs.text:
Raise controlplane.replicaCount and dataplane.replicaCount for availability and throughput. Both planes keep their state in PostgreSQL, so replicas share the work. With more than one control plane replica the chart disables the DID service self-deregistration, so that one pod shutting down does not remove the connector from the DID document.

Do not use autoscaling.enabled: its templates use the autoscaling/v2beta1 API, which current Kubernetes no longer serves. Scale with replicaCount. See Resources and scaling.

docs.title: 4. State machines (control plane)
docs.text:
Contract negotiations and transfer processes are driven by state machines that pick up a batch of entities from the database, process them, and wait before the next round.

Setting (prefix + suffix) Default Effect <prefix>.state-machine.batch-size 20 Entities processed per round. Higher means more throughput and more database load. <prefix>.state-machine.iteration-wait-millis 1000 Pause between rounds when there is nothing to do. Lower means faster reactions and more polling. <prefix>.send.retry.limit upstream default How often a failed message to the partner is retried. <prefix>.send.retry.base-delay.ms upstream default Base of the exponential backoff between retries.

The prefixes are edc.negotiation.consumer and edc.negotiation.provider for contract negotiations, and edc.transfer for transfer processes. Raise the batch size when negotiations or transfers queue up (many entities in REQUESTING, STARTING or similar states for a long time), and only together with database capacity.

docs.title: 5. Database connections
docs.text:
Each plane uses a connection pool per data source (default in the chart):

Setting Effect edc.datasource.default.pool.connections.max-total Upper limit of open connections per pod edc.datasource.default.pool.connections.max-idle Connections kept open when idle edc.datasource.default.pool.connections.min-idle Connections opened in advance edc.sql.fetch.size Rows fetched per round trip in queries

Keep max-total × replicas of both planes below the max_connections of your PostgreSQL, with room for migrations and your own tools. A bigger state machine batch needs more connections.

docs.title: 6. Caches and timeouts
docs.text: Setting Chart value Effect dcp.cache.enabled, dcp.cache.validity true, 86400 s Caches partners' verifiable presentations, saving a call to their wallet on every request. Shorter means revoked credentials are noticed sooner. controlplane.bdrs.cache_validity_seconds 600 How long the BPN ↔ DID directory is cached (Catena-X). edc.http.client.timeout.connect, edc.http.client.timeout.read upstream default Timeouts of outgoing HTTP calls (partners, wallet, BDRS). Raise when partners are slow, rather than retrying more. edc.dataplane.transfer.threads upstream default Threads of the data plane for push transfers. tx.edc.dataplane.token.expiry 300 s Lifetime of access tokens for pull transfers; longer means fewer refreshes.

docs.title: 7. Measure again
docs.text:
• Follow negotiations and transfers per state with the Management API queries.
  • Export JVM and HTTP metrics through OpenTelemetry.
  • Run a load test in a test environment with your real policies: policy evaluation and credential checks dominate the cost of a negotiation.

Like any open-source software, Tractus-X EDC comes without warranty: you are responsible for sizing and operating it. Share what you learn in the Connector Open Meeting.
