docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
The skills are the procedures and scripts the Connector Sensei works with. Each one is a folder in .claude/skills/ with a SKILL.md, which Claude Code and GitHub Copilot load when a request matches its description, and usually a scripts/ folder with a tested, read-only script you can also run yourself. How the skills work explains the idea.

This page and the pages of the skills are generated from the SKILL.md files when the site is built.

Skill Use it for Scripts edc-upstream-sources Read, search and diff upstream Eclipse EDC (org.eclipse.edc) source code and SQL schemas at the exact version Tractus-X EDC depends on, or any other version. edc-src.sh upstream-edc-bump Upgrade Tractus-X EDC to a new upstream Eclipse EDC version (the edc entry in gradle/libs.versions.toml). bump-impact.sh setting-lifecycle Add, rename, deprecate, remove or look up a Tractus-X EDC configuration setting end to end, covering the @Setting declaration, env var, Helm template, values.yaml, helm-docs README, extension README, migration guide and tests. setting-trace.sh breaking-change-guard Review a Tractus-X EDC change set (branch, PR or working tree) for changes that break operators, adopters or other dataspace participants, and for missing follow-ups. bc-scan.sh new-extension Create a new Tractus-X EDC extension or SPI module the way this repository does it. scaffold-extension.sh sql-migration Create, review or debug Tractus-X EDC PostgreSQL Flyway migrations (edc-extensions/migrations). migrations.sh e2e-test-author Write, run and debug Tractus-X EDC end-to-end tests (edc-tests/e2e/*) that start real consumer and provider connector runtimes, with Postgres, DCP, Kafka or cloud storage via Testcontainers. e2e.sh management-api-endpoint Add, change, version or deprecate a Tractus-X EDC HTTP endpoint (Management API extensions such as /v3/edrs, /v3/business-partner-groups, /v3/connectordiscovery, /v3/dataflows, or data plane public, proxy and token APIs). api-inventory.sh migration-guide-and-adr Write Tractus-X EDC migration guides (docs/migration/.md) and architecture decision records (docs/development/decision-records//README.md) in the repository's exact format, drafted from evidence (breaking-change scan, upstream version change, new DB migrations, commits since the last release). draft-migration-guide.sh, new-adr.sh dependencies-and-dash Check third-party dependency licenses for Tractus-X EDC with Eclipse Dash before merging. dash-check.sh

Planned skills are described in the skills catalog.

docs.title: EDC upstream sources
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Read, search and diff upstream Eclipse EDC (org.eclipse.edc) source code and SQL schemas at the exact version Tractus-X EDC depends on, or any other version. Use whenever an answer or change depends on upstream behaviour, such as an SPI signature, a default implementation, a state machine, a @Setting key, a JSON-LD transformer, a DSP/DCP implementation or a store schema, instead of answering from memory or from a local clone on the wrong version.

Scripts: edc-src.sh · Source: .claude/skills/edc-upstream-sources/SKILL.md

Tractus-X EDC is a distribution of upstream EDC. Most behaviour lives upstream, and upstream changes quickly. This skill gives exact, version-pinned access to upstream code without cloning anything.

The script scripts/edc-src.sh: - reads the pinned version from gradle/libs.versions.toml (edc = "…") - takes sources jars from the local Gradle cache and downloads missing ones from Maven Central - extracts them once to ~/.cache/edc-sources/<version>/<artifact>/ (override with EDC_SRC_CACHE), never into the repository

The first run per version takes up to a minute; later runs are instant. Set EDC_SRC_OFFLINE=1 to forbid downloads.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Run from anywhere inside the repository:

S=.claude/skills/edc-upstream-sources/scripts/edc-src.sh
$S version                                   # pinned upstream version, e.g. 0.17.0
$S find ContractNegotiationManager           # artifact + path of every matching source file
$S read DcpIdentityService                   # print the best match with line numbers (other matches listed)
$S read 'runtime/metamodel/annotation/Setting'   # disambiguate with a path fragment
$S grep 'implements PolicyEngine'            # extended-regex search across all upstream sources
$S settings 'edc.participant'                # upstream @Setting keys (filter is a regex)
$S schema                                    # list upstream SQL store schemas
$S schema contract-negotiation               # print one schema
$S diff EndpointDataReferenceEntry 0.16.0 0.17.0   # unified diff of a class between versions
$S path 0.16.0                               # extract another version and print its directory

To compare schemas between versions: diff <($S schema transfer-process 0.16.0) <($S schema transfer-process 0.17.0).

docs.title: How to use it well
docs.text:
1. Pin first. Run $S version and quote it in your answer ("in EDC 0.17.0, X does …").
  2. Cite precisely as org.eclipse.edc:<artifact>:<version> plus the path and line from read output, e.g. org.eclipse.edc:decentralized-claims-service:0.17.0 → org/eclipse/edc/iam/decentralizedclaims/service/DcpIdentityService.java:62.
  3. Follow the call chain. Start from the Tractus-X class (git grep), find the upstream type it imports, read it, then grep for implementations (implements <Type>) and registrations (@Provider, register().
  4. Know the local overrides. Some org.eclipse.edc.* packages are defined in this repo, mainly the DSP 0.8 backports under edc-extensions/dsp/*-08 and spi/dsp-spi-08. If find returns nothing, run git ls-files '*/<Class>.java' before concluding a type does not exist.
  5. Cover other groups. Artifacts outside org.eclipse.edc (for example org.eclipse.edc.aws) are not indexed. Read them from GitHub at the matching tag instead: https://github.com/eclipse-edc/<Repo>/tree/v<version>.
  6. Treat local clones with care. A sibling clone such as ~/eclipse-edc/Connector may be on another version. Prefer this skill, or use git -C <clone> show v<version>:<path>.

docs.title: Typical questions this answers
docs.text:
• "Which policy scope does upstream evaluate on a catalog request?" grep for CatalogPolicyContext and read the evaluating service.
  • "What does setting edc.x.y default to?" settings edc.x.y lists the key; grep '"edc\.x\.y"' finds the declaration with its defaultValue.
  • "Did upstream change the transfer-process table?" schema transfer-process in both versions, then diff.
  • "Why does my extension's override not apply?" read the default @Provider upstream and check whether it is isDefault = true.

docs.title: Upstream EDC bump
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Upgrade Tractus-X EDC to a new upstream Eclipse EDC version (the edc entry in gradle/libs.versions.toml). Use for "bump EDC to 0.x", "adapt to upstream changes", failures after a dependabot EDC bump, or planning the effort of an upcoming upstream release. Covers impact analysis, compile fixes, DSP 0.8 backports, SQL migrations, settings, tests, migration guide and license check.

Scripts: bump-impact.sh · Source: .claude/skills/upstream-edc-bump/SKILL.md

Upstream bumps are the largest recurring change in this repo. The 0.16.0 adaptation touched 59 files and the 0.17.0 one touched 25, followed by test and participant-context fixes. Work through the steps in order and keep a running checklist in the PR description.

Use the edc-upstream-sources skill throughout (.claude/skills/edc-upstream-sources/scripts/edc-src.sh).

docs.title: 1. Analyse before touching anything
docs.text:
OLD=$(.claude/skills/edc-upstream-sources/scripts/edc-src.sh version); NEW=0.18.0   # target
.claude/skills/upstream-edc-bump/scripts/bump-impact.sh "$OLD" "$NEW" --main-only   # summary
.claude/skills/upstream-edc-bump/scripts/bump-impact.sh "$OLD" "$NEW" --diff > /tmp/edc-bump.diff  # full diffs incl. tests

The report lists: - upstream types Tractus-X imports that were removed, moved or changed, ranked by how many Tractus-X files use them - upstream settings removed or added, and removed ones Tractus-X still references - upstream SQL schema changes. Each one needs a new Tractus-X Flyway migration. - links to the release notes and the GitHub compare view

Read the upstream release notes and any breaking-change or deprecation notes there. Summarise the plan, with the expected touchpoints, before you edit.

docs.title: 2. Bump the versions
docs.text: Work on a branch cut from origin/main (for example chore/upgrade-edc-$NEW). In gradle/libs.versions.toml: - set edc to the new version - check whether edc-build (the Gradle plugin) needs a matching bump - check whether dsp-tck or dcp-tck need a bump when the protocol or TCK changed - fix renamed or split artifacts, including the BOMs edc-bom-*. bump-impact "NOT FOUND" lines and Gradle resolution errors point to them.

docs.title: 3. Make it compile
docs.text:
./gradlew compileJava compileTestJava compileTestFixturesJava --continue 2>&1 | grep -E 'error:|e: ' | sort | uniq -c

For every failing type, run edc-src.sh diff <Type> $OLD $NEW and adapt. Do not copy upstream code into Tractus-X unless you are deliberately overriding it. Patterns seen in past bumps: - Participant context is passed explicitly (participantContextId) into services and stores. - Deprecated APIs or types are flagged with @Deprecated(since = …); plan their replacement. - Constructor or builder changes in TransferProcess, ContractAgreement and DataFlowStartMessage.

docs.title: 4. Behaviour, not just signatures
docs.text: Review every CHANGED type that Tractus-X overrides or wraps, not only the ones that broke the build: - DSP 0.8 backports (edc-extensions/dsp/*-08, spi/dsp-spi-08) mirror upstream DSP modules. Diff the upstream dsp-* counterparts and port fixes that still apply to 0.8. Wire format must not change within a DSP version (ADR docs/development/decision-records/2025-02-12-dsp-downward-compatibility). - DCP (edc-extensions/dcp/*): scope handling, presentation verification, STS client. - Policy (cx-policy): policy context classes, PolicyEngine registration, validator APIs. - EDR and token refresh (edr/*, dataplane-token-refresh, tokenrefresh-handler). - Monitor/logging (log4j2-monitor), when Monitor changed.

docs.title: 5. Database
docs.text: For every upstream schema change in the report, add a new migration to edc-extensions/migrations/connector-migration (src/main/resources/migrations/connector/). That module holds the shared control-plane and data-plane schema the official chart uses; the 0.17 bump added V1_9_0__Add_ClaimsColumn.sql there for exactly the claims columns the report shows. Check git log of control-plane-migration and data-plane-migration to see whether the split-schema modules still need the same change. Use the next free V…__Description.sql and never edit a released one (breaking-change-guard checks both). Keep migrations idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS). Run: ./gradlew test -DincludeTags="PostgresqlIntegrationTest". The upgradeability-test workflow covers the rest.

docs.title: 6. Settings and Helm
docs.text: For each upstream setting removed, added or renamed that operators touch, use the setting-lifecycle skill. It covers the env var in charts/*/templates, values.yaml, helm-docs and the migration-guide row.

docs.title: 7. Tests
docs.text:
Run the suites CI runs (.github/workflows/verify.yaml), cheapest first:

./gradlew test                                            # unit tests
./gradlew test -DincludeTags="ComponentTest"
./gradlew test -DincludeTags="ApiTest"
./gradlew test -DincludeTags="PostgresqlIntegrationTest"
./gradlew -p edc-tests/e2e/<suite> test -DincludeTags="EndToEndTest"   # transfer, policy, dcp, edr-api, catalog, …
./gradlew test -DincludeTags="CompatibilityTest"          # old vs new connector

Also run the dsp-tck-tests and dcp-tck-tests e2e suites. Fix fixtures in edc-tests/e2e-fixtures, which upstream changes break most often, rather than weakening assertions.

docs.title: 8. Docs and compliance
docs.text:
• Add a section to the upcoming docs/migration/<date>-Version_<x>_<y>.md covering operator-visible changes, setting and Helm renames, DB migrations and API changes.
  • Run .claude/skills/dependencies-and-dash/scripts/dash-check.sh when third-party versions moved. New restricted licenses must be cleared before release. CI regenerates DEPENDENCIES on main; do not edit it by hand.
  • Regenerate OpenAPI YAML in resources/openapi/yaml when Tractus-X API modules changed (swagger config in build.gradle.kts).
  • Finish with .claude/skills/breaking-change-guard/scripts/bc-scan.sh and resolve or justify every finding.

Commit message convention: chore: update to upstream EDC <version> and do necessary adaptations.

docs.title: Setting lifecycle
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Add, rename, deprecate, remove or look up a Tractus-X EDC configuration setting end to end, covering the @Setting declaration, env var, Helm template, values.yaml, helm-docs README, extension README, migration guide and tests. Use for "what is the env var / Helm value for X", "add a config option", "rename this setting", "why is my setting ignored", or any change touching charts/*/values.yaml.

Scripts: setting-trace.sh · Source: .claude/skills/setting-lifecycle/SKILL.md

A connector setting usually lives in up to seven places. Most migration-guide content in docs/migration/ is old→new tables for settings and Helm values, so missing one place is the most common review comment and operator-facing bug.

# Place Example 1 @Setting declaration (Tractus-X or upstream) BdrsClientExtension.java: @Setting(key = BDRS_SERVER_URL_PROPERTY, …) 2 Env var name tx.edc.iam.dcp.bdrs.server.url → TX_EDC_IAM_DCP_BDRS_SERVER_URL (upper-case, . and - → _) 3 Helm template that sets it charts/tractusx-connector/templates/deployment-controlplane.yaml (and -dataplane, plus tractusx-connector-memory/templates/deployment-runtime.yaml) 4 Helm value charts/*/values.yaml, with a # -- comment that helm-docs renders 5 Chart README charts/*/README.md, generated by helm-docs from README.md.gotmpl and verified in CI 6 Extension README edc-extensions/<ext>/README.md ## Configuration table 7 Migration guide docs/migration/<date>-Version_<x>_<y>.md for renames, removals, default changes

docs.title: Step 0: trace what exists
docs.text:
.claude/skills/setting-lifecycle/scripts/setting-trace.sh tx.edc.iam.dcp.bdrs.server.url
.claude/skills/setting-lifecycle/scripts/setting-trace.sh EDC_PARTICIPANT_ID
.claude/skills/setting-lifecycle/scripts/setting-trace.sh .Values.controlplane.bdrs.cache_validity_seconds

It resolves key ↔ env var ↔ Helm path, shows the declaration (Tractus-X and upstream at the pinned version), the template lines, the values.yaml entries in every chart, the docs, the migration history and the tests. It ends with a touchpoint checklist.

docs.title: Adding a setting
docs.text:
1. Declare it on the extension that consumes it: 
    static final String FOO_TIMEOUT = "tx.edc.foo.timeout";
@Setting(key = FOO_TIMEOUT, description = "Timeout in seconds for …", defaultValue = "30")
private int timeout;
  2. Prefixes: tx.edc.* for Tractus-X features, tractusx.edc.* for participant identity, and edc.* only when you configure an upstream setting.
  3. Use required = false or a defaultValue unless the runtime cannot start without it.
  4. For grouped settings consider a @Settings record (see upstream edc-src.sh grep '@Settings').
  5. Expose it in the chart only if operators need it. Add the env var under the right plane's env: block, guarded when optional: 
    {{- if .Values.controlplane.foo.timeout }}
- name: "TX_EDC_FOO_TIMEOUT"
  value: {{ .Values.controlplane.foo.timeout | quote }}
{{- end }}
    Add the value with a helm-docs comment in each chart (tractusx-connector uses controlplane.* / dataplane.*; tractusx-connector-memory uses runtime.*): 
    foo:
  # -- Timeout in seconds for …
  timeout: 30
  6. Regenerate the chart READMEs: docker run --rm -v "$PWD/charts:/helm-docs" jnorwood/helm-docs helm-docs (the same command as CI's verify-helm-docs).
  7. Document it in the extension README configuration table.
  8. Test it: an extension test with ConfigFactory.fromMap(Map.of(FOO_TIMEOUT, "5")), and a Helm template test in charts/*/templates/tests when the template logic is non-trivial.

docs.title: Renaming a setting (deprecate, then remove)
docs.text:
Never rename in one step. Tractus-X deprecates first and removes in a later release; for example the 0.13 guide removed settings deprecated since 0.8.

  1. Keep the old key working: read the new key and fall back to the old one with a warning: 
    @Deprecated(since = "0.14.0")
static final String OLD_KEY = "tx.edc.old.key";
static final String NEW_KEY = "tx.edc.new.key";
…
var value = config.getString(NEW_KEY, null);
if (value == null && config.hasKey(OLD_KEY)) {
    monitor.warning("Setting '%s' is deprecated, use '%s' instead".formatted(OLD_KEY, NEW_KEY));
    value = config.getString(OLD_KEY);
}
  2. In the chart, emit the new env var and accept the old value as a fallback: {{ .Values.new.path | default .Values.old.path }}. Keep the old value commented as deprecated in values.yaml.
  3. Add a migration-guide row in the established format: | Old value | New value | New environment variable | (or the Old Helm value | New Helm value table).
  4. Removal later: delete the fallback and the old Helm value, and note the removal in that release's guide.

docs.title: Removing or changing a default
docs.text: These are breaking for operators. Add a migration-guide entry, run .claude/skills/breaking-change-guard/scripts/bc-scan.sh, and mention it in the PR description.

docs.title: Debugging "my setting is ignored"
docs.text:
1. Trace it and confirm the env var name is spelled exactly as derived from the key.
  2. Check that the setting is consumed by the right runtime (control plane vs data plane) and that the extension is in that runtime's build.gradle.kts.
  3. Check whether upstream also declares the key (the trace shows it); an upstream @Setting may win or differ in default.
  4. Check where the value is read. Since EDC 0.15 some services read configuration through the participant context (ParticipantContextConfig, single-participant store in participant-context-connector-classic-core) rather than context.getConfig(). Use edc-src.sh grep on the key to see which path applies.

docs.title: Breaking-change guard
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Review a Tractus-X EDC change set (branch, PR or working tree) for changes that break operators, adopters or other dataspace participants, and for missing follow-ups. Covers released SQL migrations, settings, Helm values and env vars, Management API paths, JSON-LD contexts, DSP/DCP wire behaviour, public SPIs, runtime composition, migration guide, helm-docs and license check. Use before opening or approving a PR, when reviewing someone's PR, or when asked "is this breaking?".

Scripts: bc-scan.sh · Source: .claude/skills/breaking-change-guard/SKILL.md

Catena-X participants must be able to keep exchanging data when the other side upgrades (CX operating model). Within a DSP version the connector must stay strictly backward compatible (ADR docs/development/decision-records/2025-02-12-dsp-downward-compatibility). Operators rely on the migration guides to upgrade. This skill finds what a change breaks and what still has to be written.

docs.title: 1. Scan
docs.text:
.claude/skills/breaking-change-guard/scripts/bc-scan.sh                 # vs origin/main, incl. uncommitted work
.claude/skills/breaking-change-guard/scripts/bc-scan.sh <base-ref>      # e.g. a release tag or the PR base
.claude/skills/breaking-change-guard/scripts/bc-scan.sh --strict        # exit 1 on BLOCKER/BREAKING (CI-style)

To review a PR: gh pr checkout <n>, then run the scan against its base (gh pr view <n> --json baseRefName).

Severity Meaning Examples the scanner detects BLOCKER Must not merge as is A Flyway migration shipped in the latest release was modified or removed; duplicate or out-of-order migration version BREAKING Operators or clients break unless handled Setting key removed or renamed; Helm value subtree removed; env var no longer set by the chart; @Path removed HIGH Wire or data compatibility risk; needs targeted tests DSP or DCP implementation changed; JSON-LD context or namespace URL changed; new DB migration; upstream EDC bumped WARN Follow-up missing No migration-guide change; chart README not regenerated; third-party dependencies changed without a license check; new setting undocumented; SPI signature changed; feature removed from a runtime

The scanner is a heuristic. Treat each finding as a question, confirm it by reading the diff, and look beyond it (step 2).

docs.title: 2. Judge what the scanner cannot see
docs.text:
• JSON-LD and DTO shape. Did a Management API response or a DSP message gain, lose or rename a property, or change its @type or compaction? Additions are usually fine; removals and renames are breaking. For DSP, compare against the compatibility test expectations in edc-tests/compatibility-tests.
  • Semantics. Changed defaults, policy evaluation (which scope, which leftOperand accepted), state-machine transitions, retry or timeouts, token lifetimes, and error codes (ADR 2025-07-21-return-http-status-codes-in-dataplane).
  • Persistence. Columns read by older connector versions during rolling upgrades, or JSON stored in columns (for example policies and data addresses) whose structure changed.
  • Security posture. Auth on a newly exposed endpoint, secrets in logs, sender-constrained tokens.
  • Multi-dataspace boundary. Catena-X specifics leaking into generic core/tx-* modules, or the reverse (ADR 2026-01-07_multi-dataspace-support).

docs.title: 3. Required follow-ups for a breaking or high finding
docs.text:
1. Avoid the break if possible. Deprecate instead of removing (see the setting-lifecycle skill), keep the old API path alongside the new one for at least one release (as with v4alpha → v3), and add a new migration instead of editing a released one.
  2. Migration guide. Add to the upcoming docs/migration/<date>-Version_<x>_<y>.md. Keep its table of contents, one numbered section per topic, and old→new tables with the env var column. Look at the latest guide for the exact style.
  3. Tests that prove compatibility:
  4. DSP: ./gradlew test -DincludeTags="CompatibilityTest" and the edc-tests/e2e/dsp-tck-tests suite
  5. DCP: edc-tests/e2e/dcp-tests, dcp-tck-tests
  6. DB: -DincludeTags="PostgresqlIntegrationTest", plus the upgradeability-test workflow
  7. API: -DincludeTags="ApiTest" and management-tests
  8. Housekeeping. Run helm-docs for chart changes, run the dependencies-and-dash skill for new third-party artifacts, update the OpenAPI YAML for API changes, and add a decision record for architectural changes (docs/development/decision-records/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<topic>/README.md).

docs.title: 4. Report
docs.text: Summarise as a table: finding, severity, evidence (path:line), and resolution (fixed, justified, or follow-up issue). In a PR review, post BLOCKER and BREAKING items as review comments on the exact lines.

docs.title: New extension
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Create a new Tractus-X EDC extension or SPI module the way this repository does it. Covers the generic-vs-Catena-X placement decision, module scaffold with license headers, ServiceExtension with @Extension/@Inject/@Provider/@Setting, META-INF service registration, a DependencyInjectionExtension test, README, settings.gradle.kts include and wiring into the control-plane or data-plane runtime. Use for "add an extension", "new module", "where should this feature live", or when splitting an extension into core and cx- parts.

Scripts: scaffold-extension.sh · Source: .claude/skills/new-extension/SKILL.md

docs.title: 1. Decide where it lives (before writing code)
docs.text:
Tractus-X EDC is becoming a midstream for several dataspaces (ADR docs/development/decision-records/2026-01-07_multi-dataspace-support). Classify the feature first:

Category Belongs in Naming Examples Generic, dataspace-agnostic edc-extensions/<feature> or <feature>/<feature>-core tx-… or no prefix agreements, dcp/tx-dcp, event-subscriber Catena-X specific (BPN, CX policies, CX credentials) sibling cx-… module cx-… cx-policy, dcp/cx-dcp, connector-discovery/cx-connector-discovery Contract other modules implement spi/<feature>-spi or edc-extensions/<feature>/<feature>-spi …-spi spi/edr-spi, bpn-validation/bpn-validation-spi Upstream behaviour that belongs upstream contribute to eclipse-edc instead

If a generic feature needs Catena-X behaviour, put an interface in the generic module and the Catena-X implementation in the cx- module, as dcp/tx-dcp + dcp/cx-dcp do. New dataspace flavours are developed outside this repo first, per the ADR.

Check for an existing extension you can extend: ls edc-extensions spi, and check upstream with the edc-upstream-sources skill (edc-src.sh grep 'interface <Concept>').

docs.title: 2. Scaffold
docs.text:
.claude/skills/new-extension/scripts/scaffold-extension.sh \
  edc-extensions/cx-foo  org.eclipse.tractusx.edc.foo  CxFooExtension  tx.edc.foo

It creates, and never overwrites: - build.gradle.kts - <CxFoo>Extension.java, with an enabled @Setting and an injected Monitor - META-INF/services/org.eclipse.edc.spi.system.ServiceExtension - <CxFoo>ExtensionTest.java, using DependencyInjectionExtension - README.md, with a configuration table

All files carry license headers that pass Checkstyle (resources/java.header, resources/hashtag.header). The generated module builds green as is: compile, Checkstyle on main and test, and the unit test.

Then do what the script prints: 1. Add include(":edc-extensions:cx-foo") to settings.gradle.kts, next to related modules. 2. Ship it with implementation(project(":edc-extensions:cx-foo")) in edc-controlplane/edc-controlplane-base/build.gradle.kts or edc-dataplane/edc-dataplane-base/build.gradle.kts. Leave it out if it is opt-in for adopters building their own runtime. 3. Replace libs.edc.spi.core with the SPIs you actually use (aliases in gradle/libs.versions.toml, e.g. libs.edc.spi.policyengine, libs.edc.spi.controlplane). Use api(…) only for types exposed in your public signatures.

docs.title: 3. Implement with EDC idioms
docs.text:
• Inject collaborators with @Inject (or @Inject(required = false) when optional). Never look services up manually.
  • Provide services with @Provider methods. Use @Provider(isDefault = true) for defaults that other extensions may override, typically in-memory defaults that SQL extensions replace.
  • Configure with @Setting(key = CONST, description = …, defaultValue = …) on fields, or a @Settings record. Follow the setting-lifecycle skill if operators need a Helm value.
  • Register, don't wire. Use policy functions via PolicyEngine.registerFunction(<Context>.class, …), rule bindings via RuleBindingRegistry, JSON-LD transformers via TypeTransformerRegistry, validators via JsonObjectValidatorRegistry, and API controllers via WebService.registerResource(<ApiContext>, …).
  • JSON-LD. Use terms from spi/core-spi/.../CoreConstants (TX_NAMESPACE, CX_POLICY_2025_09_NS, …) and cached contexts in core/json-ld-*. Never invent namespaces.
  • Results, not exceptions. Return ServiceResult, StoreResult and Result across boundaries, as upstream does.
  • Logging. Inject Monitor and never log secrets or tokens (ADR 2025-07-09-logging_and_metrics_strategy).
  • Persistence. For SQL stores, follow edr-index-lock-sql and bpns-evaluation-store-sql: a …Statements interface, a Postgres dialect class, @Setting for the datasource name, and a Flyway migration in edc-extensions/migrations/connector-migration.

docs.title: 4. Test like the repo does
docs.text:
• Unit tests next to the code with JUnit 5 + AssertJ + Mockito. Extension wiring uses @ExtendWith(DependencyInjectionExtension.class) (see the generated test).
  • Tag slower tests: @ComponentTest, @ApiTest, @PostgresqlIntegrationTest, @EndToEndTest. CI runs them by tag (.github/workflows/verify.yaml).
  • End-to-end: add a case to the matching suite in edc-tests/e2e/*, reusing participants and helpers from edc-tests/e2e-fixtures (TractusxParticipantBase, Runtimes, PostgresExtension, PolicyHelperFunctions, …).

docs.title: 5. Finish
docs.text:
• ./gradlew :edc-extensions:cx-foo:build passes, which includes Checkstyle.
  • README documents purpose, plane, dataspace category and every setting.
  • New third-party dependencies are added to gradle/libs.versions.toml and pass the license check (dependencies-and-dash skill). CI regenerates DEPENDENCIES on main, so do not edit it by hand.
  • Run the breaking-change-guard scan.
  • Commit with Conventional Commits, e.g. feat(cx-foo): add ….

docs.title: SQL migration
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Create, review or debug Tractus-X EDC PostgreSQL Flyway migrations (edc-extensions/migrations). Use when a store's schema changes (new column, index, table, data fix), when upstream EDC changed a store schema, when a connector fails at startup with a Flyway or "column does not exist" error, or when asked which migration version comes next.

Scripts: migrations.sh · Source: .claude/skills/sql-migration/SKILL.md

Tractus-X EDC owns the database schema of the connector. Upstream EDC ships *-schema.sql files but no migrations, so every upstream schema change needs a Tractus-X Flyway migration. Released migrations are immutable: Flyway checksums them, and a modified file breaks every existing deployment on startup.

docs.title: Where migrations live
docs.text:
Module Folder Used by connector-migration src/main/resources/migrations/connector/ (V1_<n>_0__…) The official charts: control plane and data plane share one schema. Put new work here. control-plane-migration …/postgresql/migration/<store>/ (V0_0_<n>__…) Split-schema deployments, one folder per store (asset, policy, contractnegotiation, transferprocess, …) data-plane-migration …/postgresql/migration/<store>/ Split-schema data plane (dataplane, accesstokendata) postgresql-migration-lib Java only AbstractPostgresqlMigrationExtension, FlywayManager, DatabaseMigrationConfiguration

Each store can be switched off with tx.edc.postgresql.migration.<store>.enabled=false, and the schema is set with tx.edc.postgresql.migration.schema. See the module READMEs.

docs.title: 1. Look before you write
docs.text:
.claude/skills/sql-migration/scripts/migrations.sh status       # every folder: count, latest, released in <latest tag>?
.claude/skills/sql-migration/scripts/migrations.sh next connector
.claude/skills/edc-upstream-sources/scripts/edc-src.sh schema transfer-process   # upstream target schema

When the change comes from an upstream bump, upstream-edc-bump/scripts/bump-impact.sh lists the exact schema deltas. In the 0.17 bump these were the claims columns on edc_contract_agreement and edc_transfer_process, which became V1_9_0__Add_ClaimsColumn.sql.

docs.title: 2. Create the migration
docs.text:
.claude/skills/sql-migration/scripts/migrations.sh new connector "Add data address alias"
# -> .../migrations/connector/V1_10_0__Add_Data_Address_Alias.sql with license header and a TODO body

The script picks the next version per folder, bumping the minor (V1_9_0 → V1_10_0) or the patch (V0_0_6 → V0_0_7), and refuses a version that is not newer than the latest. Use --version only to fill a deliberate gap.

Write the SQL so it is idempotent and safe on large tables: - ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS …, CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS …, DROP … IF EXISTS. - Data migrations: guarded UPDATE … WHERE <old shape> so a rerun is a no-op. Cast JSON explicitly (::json) and keep the JSON structure the upstream store expects. - No destructive change to data a still-running older connector reads during a rolling upgrade. Add first, remove in a later release. - One concern per file, named by intent (Add_…, Alter_…, Remove_…).

If you also support split-schema deployments, add the equivalent change to the store folder in control-plane-migration or data-plane-migration. Check git log on that folder to see whether recent upstream changes were mirrored there.

docs.title: 3. Test
docs.text:
./gradlew :edc-extensions:migrations:connector-migration:test -DincludeTags="PostgresqlIntegrationTest"  # Docker
./gradlew test -DincludeTags="PostgresqlIntegrationTest"     # store tests against the migrated schema

ConnectorPostgresqlMigrationTest runs the full chain on Testcontainers Postgres. CI also runs the upgradeability-test workflow, which deploys the last release, upgrades it, and checks the data survives.

docs.title: 4. Review checklist
docs.text:
• No released V…__ file was modified or removed (breaking-change-guard reports this as a BLOCKER).
  • Version is unique and newer than every file in the folder (migrations.sh status shows no duplicates).
  • Statements are idempotent, and data migrations are guarded.
  • Matches the upstream *-schema.sql of the pinned EDC version.
  • Mentioned in the upcoming migration guide if operators must act: long-running migration, manual backup, or disabling a store migration (migration-guide-and-adr skill).

docs.title: Debugging startup failures
docs.text:
• Validate failed: Migration checksum mismatch: a released file was edited. Restore it from the release tag and move the change into a new file.
  • Detected resolved migration not applied or out of order: a version lower than the latest applied one was added. Renumber it.
  • column … does not exist after an upstream bump: a schema delta has no migration. Run bump-impact.sh and add it.

docs.title: E2E test author
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Write, run and debug Tractus-X EDC end-to-end tests (edc-tests/e2e/*) that start real consumer and provider connector runtimes, with Postgres, DCP, Kafka or cloud storage via Testcontainers. Use when a feature needs an end-to-end proof (catalog, policy, negotiation, transfer, EDR, token refresh, discovery, DSP/DCP TCK), when an E2E test is flaky or failing in CI, or to find which suite covers a behaviour.

Scripts: e2e.sh · Source: .claude/skills/e2e-test-author/SKILL.md

E2E tests are the executable specification of this connector. They start two full Tractus-X runtimes in the test JVM (consumer and provider) and drive them through the Management API, exactly as a participant would.

docs.title: 1. Find the right suite
docs.text:
.claude/skills/e2e-test-author/scripts/e2e.sh list
Behaviour Suite Catalog filtering by access policy, BPN and groups, DSP 0.8 vs 2025-1 catalog-tests Policy validation and evaluation, policy monitor policy-tests PULL and PUSH transfers, retirement, token refresh in transfers, dataflow API transfer-tests EDR API (/v3/edrs), negotiate-and-cache edr-api-tests Identity: DCP, STS, DIV, credential spoofing dcp-tests, dcp-tck-tests Protocol compliance dsp-tck-tests Connector discovery (/v3/connectordiscovery) discovery-tests Management API validators, delegated auth management-tests S3 and Azure, Kafka cloud-transfer-tests, end2end-transfer-cloud, kafka-transfer-tests Data plane token refresh edc-dataplane-tokenrefresh-tests BPN events bpn-event-tests

Add to an existing suite whenever the runtime setup fits. A new suite (folder, build.gradle.kts, settings.gradle.kts include) is only worth it for a new infrastructure dependency.

docs.title: 2. Use the fixtures, do not reinvent them
docs.text:
All shared code is in edc-tests/e2e-fixtures/src/testFixtures/java/org/eclipse/tractusx/edc/tests/:

Fixture Purpose participant/TransferParticipant, TractusxParticipantBase, DcpParticipant A participant: name, DID, BPN and protocol, plus Management API helpers (createAsset, createPolicyDefinition, createContractDefinition, getCatalogDatasets, edrs(), waitForTransferProcess, …) runtimes/Runtimes Runtime factories: pgRuntime(participant, postgres), discovery runtimes, … runtimes/PostgresExtension, KafkaExtension, S3MockExtension, AzuriteExtension, FlociExtension Testcontainers-backed infrastructure, registered with @RegisterExtension @Order(0) TestRuntimeConfiguration CONSUMER_* and PROVIDER_* names, DIDs, BPNs; DSP_2025, DSP_2025_PATH helpers/PolicyHelperFunctions, CatalogHelperFunctions, EdrNegotiationHelperFunctions, QueryHelperFunctions Policies in Catena-X ODRL (emptyPolicy, bpnPolicy, frameworkConstraint, …), catalog accessors, EDR negotiation, queries MockBdrsClient, MockVcIdentityService, DataspaceIssuer Identity stubs and a test issuer for DCP

When several tests need a helper, add it to the fixtures instead of copying it.

docs.title: 3. Scaffold, compile, run
docs.text:
.claude/skills/e2e-test-author/scripts/e2e.sh new catalog-tests CatalogVisibilityEndToEndTest
.claude/skills/e2e-test-author/scripts/e2e.sh compile catalog-tests          # compile + Checkstyle, no Docker
.claude/skills/e2e-test-author/scripts/e2e.sh run catalog-tests CatalogVisibility   # Docker required

The scaffold is a working provider/consumer test: Postgres runtimes, DSP 2025-1, asset → policy → contract definition → catalog assertion. Replace the scenario and keep the structure. run uses the same flags as CI (-DincludeTags="EndToEndTest" -PverboseTest=true) and fails fast when Docker is not reachable.

docs.title: 4. Write tests that stay green
docs.text:
• One behaviour per test, named <action>_<condition>_<expectation>, with a @DisplayName sentence.
  • Wait, never sleep. Use waitForTransferProcess, negotiation-state helpers, or Awaitility (await().untilAsserted). Fixed Thread.sleep is the main cause of flaky tests.
  • Unique ids per test (UUID.randomUUID()), or clean up with DataWiperExtension. Runtimes and databases are shared across the methods of a class.
  • Cover both protocol versions when behaviour is protocol-facing: TransferParticipant.Builder.protocol(...) with DSP 2025-1 and the 0.8 default (see CatalogTest vs CatalogTestDspV08).
  • Parameterise over Management API versions where both are served (see PolicyDefinitionEndToEndTest).
  • Assert on the API contract (status codes, JSON-LD fields), not on internal store state, unless the test is about persistence.

docs.title: 5. Debugging failures
docs.text:
1. Re-run just the failing class locally: e2e.sh run <suite> <Class>. Reports are in edc-tests/e2e/<suite>/build/reports/tests/test/index.html. CI uploads Allure results per suite.
  2. Read the runtime logs in the test output. Both runtimes run in the test JVM and log into the same output, so search by negotiation or transfer-process id to follow one flow across consumer and provider.
  3. Typical root causes: a policy fixture out of date with CX-0152 validation, a missing setting in TractusxParticipantBase config after an upstream change, a port clash, a Docker image pull timeout, or async state asserted without waiting.
  4. After an upstream bump, fix the fixtures (TractusxParticipantBase, Runtimes) once, rather than every test.

docs.title: Management API endpoint
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Add, change, version or deprecate a Tractus-X EDC HTTP endpoint (Management API extensions such as /v3/edrs, /v3/business-partner-groups, /v3/connectordiscovery, /v3/dataflows, or data plane public, proxy and token APIs). Covers the API interface with OpenAPI annotations, controller, JSON-LD transformers and validators, registration in an API context, API tests, the OpenAPI spec and the walkthrough docs. Use for "add an endpoint", "move v4alpha to v3", "why does my request return 400", or to list the endpoints Tractus-X adds.

Scripts: api-inventory.sh · Source: .claude/skills/management-api-endpoint/SKILL.md

Upstream EDC provides the core Management API (assets, policies, catalog, negotiations, transfers, …). Tractus-X adds its own endpoints on top, and those are the ones this skill covers. For upstream endpoints, read the upstream controllers with edc-upstream-sources (for example edc-src.sh find ContractNegotiationApiV3Controller).

docs.title: 1. Inventory first
docs.text:
.claude/skills/management-api-endpoint/scripts/api-inventory.sh            # every Tractus-X endpoint
.claude/skills/management-api-endpoint/scripts/api-inventory.sh v4alpha    # filter by path regex

For each endpoint it shows the method, full path, controller, API context (management, public, proxy, …), whether a controller test exists, whether the walkthrough in docs/usage/ mentions it, and deprecation.

docs.title: 2. Anatomy (follow the existing modules)
docs.text:
Use edc-extensions/dataplane/dataflow/dataflow-api (small) or edc-extensions/edr/edr-api-v2 (full JSON-LD) as the template:

Piece Example Notes API interface with OpenAPI annotations v3/DataFlowV3Api @OpenAPIDefinition(info = @Info(version = "v3")), @Tag, @Operation, @ApiResponse per status code. These feed the generated spec. Versioned controller v3/DataFlowV3ApiController @Path("/v3/<resource>"), @Consumes/@Produces(APPLICATION_JSON). Implements the interface and delegates to a version-independent base. Shared base logic DataFlowApiController, BaseEdrCacheApiController Keeps v3 and deprecated versions behaviourally identical. JSON-LD in and out JsonObjectTo…Transformer, JsonObjectFrom…Transformer Registered in the TypeTransformerRegistry for the management API context. Request bodies arrive expanded: read EDC_NAMESPACE/TX_NAMESPACE IRIs, not compact terms. Validation …RequestValidator Registered in JsonObjectValidatorRegistry for the @type. Invalid input → ValidationFailure 400. Errors exceptionMapper(Type.class, id) and ServiceResult ObjectNotFoundException → 404, InvalidRequestException → 400, ObjectConflictException → 409. Never return 500 for client errors. Registration …ApiExtension webService.registerResource(ApiContext.MANAGEMENT, controller). Data plane public APIs use their own context. Auth inherited from the context The Management API context is protected by the configured auth (web.http.management.auth.*, API key or delegated). A new context needs its own auth decision.

docs.title: 3. Versioning and deprecation
docs.text: The Management API path carries the version (/v3/...). The repo has done this before: moving v4alpha endpoints to v3 in 0.13 (migration guide 0.12 → 0.13, section 2). - A new endpoint goes under the current stable version (/v3/...), unless it is explicitly experimental (/v4alpha/...). - Changing a request or response shape breaks clients: add the new shape next to the old one or under a new version. - Deprecating means annotating the old interface and controller @Deprecated(since = "<version>"), keeping both registered for at least one release, adding a migration-guide row (old path → new path), and removing it later. breaking-change-guard flags a removed @Path.

docs.title: 4. Tests
docs.text:
• Controller test (@ApiTest) extending upstream RestControllerTestBase (org.eclipse.edc.web.jersey.testfixtures), with RestAssured calls against the in-process Jersey server and mocked services. See BusinessPartnerGroupApiV3ControllerTest / BaseBusinessPartnerGroupApiControllerTest.
  • Transformer and validator unit tests next to the classes (JsonObjectToConnectorDiscoveryRequestTest, …).
  • End to end through a real runtime in edc-tests/e2e/management-tests or the feature's suite (e2e-test-author skill).
  • Run ./gradlew test -DincludeTags="ApiTest" (CI job "API tests").

docs.title: 5. Spec and docs
docs.text:
• OpenAPI: ./gradlew resolve generates YAML into resources/openapi/yaml (swagger config in the root build.gradle.kts, resourcePackages = org.eclipse.tractusx.edc). publish-openapi-ui.yml publishes it, so check the generated YAML for your operation.
  • Walkthrough: add or extend a page in docs/usage/management-api-walkthrough/ with a copy-pasteable request and response. Keep JSON-LD @context complete.
  • Migration guide entry for new, changed or deprecated paths (migration-guide-and-adr skill).

docs.title: Debugging "400 Bad Request" or "ValidationFailure"
docs.text:
1. Read the response body. It lists the failing JSON-LD path and the validator message.
  2. Check the @context. Without the right context, terms do not expand to the IRIs the validator expects (https://w3id.org/edc/v0.0.1/ns/, https://w3id.org/tractusx/v0.0.1/ns/, the Catena-X policy context).
  3. Check the @type the validator is registered for. A wrong or non-expanded type skips validation silently: upstream JsonObjectValidatorRegistryImpl.validate defaults to success for unknown types (EDC 0.17.0). The failure then surfaces later, in the transformer or the service.
  4. Compare with the request in the walkthrough or the E2E test for that endpoint.

docs.title: Migration guide and ADR
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Write Tractus-X EDC migration guides (docs/migration/.md) and architecture decision records (docs/development/decision-records//README.md) in the repository's exact format, drafted from evidence (breaking-change scan, upstream version change, new DB migrations, commits since the last release). Use when preparing a release, when a PR introduces an operator-visible change, or when a design decision needs to be recorded before implementation.

Scripts: draft-migration-guide.sh, new-adr.sh · Source: .claude/skills/migration-guide-and-adr/SKILL.md

Two kinds of documents carry most of this project's knowledge: - Migration guides (docs/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>-Version_<a.b>.x_<c.d>.x.md), one per minor release. They tell operators and adopters what they must change. Most of their content is old→new tables. - Decision records (docs/development/decision-records/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<topic>/README.md). They explain why before the code lands. Recent examples: multi-dataspace support, VP caching, DID service registration, refresh-token retirement.

docs.title: 1. Draft from evidence
docs.text:
.claude/skills/migration-guide-and-adr/scripts/draft-migration-guide.sh --branch HEAD          # print the draft
.claude/skills/migration-guide-and-adr/scripts/draft-migration-guide.sh --branch HEAD --write  # create the file if absent

It compares the newest release tag (e.g. 0.13.0) with the branch and collects: - the breaking-change scan (bc-scan.sh): removed settings, Helm values and env vars, API paths, DSP/DCP and JSON-LD changes - the upstream EDC version change, if any - Flyway migrations added since the release - feat/fix/refactor commits since the release, with breaking (!) commits called out

Everything lands in an EVIDENCE comment block. Turn the relevant items into sections, then delete the block.

docs.title: 2. Write it in the house style
docs.text:
Copy the structure of the latest guide (docs/migration/2026_06-Version_0.12.x_0.13.x.md): - Title # Migration Guide \a.x -> b.x`, the standard two-paragraph intro, and alist. - **One numbered##section per topic** (## 3. Postgres Version,## 5. `IATP` renamed to `DCP``). - Tables for renames, always including the env var:

Old value New value New environment variable tx.edc.iam.iatp.bdrs.server.url tx.edc.iam.dcp.bdrs.server.url TX_EDC_IAM_DCP_BDRS_SERVER_URL

and for Helm: | Old Helm value | New Helm value |, plus API paths: | Old API | New API |. - Say what operators must do and what happens if they don't. Mark mandatory steps with > [!IMPORTANT]. - Link the extension README or decision record for details. Do not repeat them. - Upstream changes appear only where operators or adopters notice them.

Use setting-lifecycle/scripts/setting-trace.sh <old-key> to fill rename rows accurately (key, env var, Helm path).

docs.title: Decision record
docs.text:
.claude/skills/migration-guide-and-adr/scripts/new-adr.sh "Verifiable presentation cache eviction" --holder "Cofinity-X GmbH"

This creates docs/development/decision-records/<today>-<slug>/README.md with the structure the records use:

  • # Title
  • ## Decision: what will be done, in one paragraph.
  • ## Rationale: why, with the constraints (CX standards, DSP/DCP specs, upstream behaviour) and rejected alternatives.
  • ## Approach: SPIs and extensions (generic vs cx-), configuration, API, persistence, compatibility. Optional ### … subsections and diagrams (mermaid is used in existing records).
  • ## NOTICE: CC-BY-4.0, with SPDX-FileCopyrightText: <year> <holder>.

The script also lists existing records with overlapping words, so a decision can reference or supersede them.

Process: open the decision record as its own PR (docs: …) for review before the implementation PR. The implementation PR links it, and the migration guide links it when the change is operator-visible.

docs.title: Checklist before a release
docs.text:
• draft-migration-guide.sh evidence is fully triaged: each item is in the guide or consciously dropped.
  • Every removed or renamed setting, Helm value, env var and API path has a table row.
  • DB migrations that need operator attention are explained.
  • Upstream EDC bump consequences are covered.
  • The TOC matches the sections, and links resolve.

docs.title: Dependencies and Eclipse Dash
docs.text:
Connector Sensei skill

When it is used: Check third-party dependency licenses for Tractus-X EDC with Eclipse Dash before merging. Reproduces CI's dependency list for the published control plane and data plane, diffs it against the DEPENDENCIES file CI publishes, runs Dash, and explains how to resolve restricted or rejected dependencies. Use when adding or bumping a library, when a dependabot PR or the release's dependency check fails, or when asked about DEPENDENCIES or Eclipse IP.

Scripts: dash-check.sh · Source: .claude/skills/dependencies-and-dash/SKILL.md

Every third-party artifact shipped in the Tractus-X EDC images must be license-vetted by the Eclipse Foundation (Eclipse Dash License Tool, IP due diligence). In this repository:

  • DEPENDENCIES is generated, not hand-edited. .github/workflows/generate-and-publish-dependencies.yaml runs on every push to main and release/*. It builds the list (.github/actions/generate-and-check-dependencies), runs Dash (eclipse-tractusx/sig-infra run-dash, Dash 1.1.0) and publishes the result to https://eclipse-tractusx.github.io/tractusx-edc/DEPENDENCIES. The committed file on main can be empty.
  • Releases are strict. For official releases the check runs with fail_on_restricted. A restricted dependency that slipped in on main blocks the release, not the PR that introduced it, so check in the PR.

docs.title: 1. Check locally
docs.text:
.claude/skills/dependencies-and-dash/scripts/dash-check.sh --list-only   # ~10 s: list + diff vs published file
.claude/skills/dependencies-and-dash/scripts/dash-check.sh               # ~40 s: also runs Eclipse Dash 1.1.0

The script: 1. Builds the dependency list exactly like CI: :edc-controlplane:allDependencies and :edc-dataplane:allDependencies on runtimeClasspath, with the same coordinate extraction. 2. Diffs it against the published DEPENDENCIES: new artifacts or versions your branch introduces, and ones no longer used. 3. Lists dependencies that are already restricted upstream (pending IP review). 4. Runs Dash and reports approved, restricted and rejected counts. Outputs go to a temp dir; the repository is never modified.

docs.title: 2. Resolve findings
docs.text:
Status Meaning What to do approved License vetted (ClearlyDefined or an IP issue) Nothing restricted Not yet vetted, or the license is unclear Prefer a version that is already approved. Otherwise get it reviewed: a committer runs Dash with -review -project automotive.tractusx -token <gitlab-token> to open an IP issue at gitlab.eclipse.org, or you harvest it on https://clearlydefined.io/harvest and wait for the curation. Track it in the PR. rejected License incompatible with EPL/Apache distribution Do not ship it. Find an alternative, or remove the transitive path (exclude(...) in Gradle).

Other levers: - Pin or align versions in gradle/libs.versions.toml. A version bump can turn an approved artifact into a restricted one, because approval is per version. The repo already forces some versions (e.g. com.networknt:json-schema-validator via resolutionStrategy). - Find who pulls a transitive artifact: ./gradlew :edc-controlplane:edc-controlplane-base:dependencyInsight --configuration runtimeClasspath --dependency <artifact>. - Only shipped runtimes count. Test-only dependencies (Testcontainers, WireMock, …) are not in the published list, but stay sensible.

docs.title: 3. In a PR
docs.text:
• dash-check.sh shows no new restricted or rejected entries, or each one has an IP review link.
  • Do not commit a regenerated DEPENDENCIES; CI owns it.
  • For dependabot PRs, the new version is listed as approved (or reviewed) before merge.

Background: docs/development/release.md (manual Dash procedure, which this script automates) and the Eclipse handbook on IP due diligence (https://www.eclipse.org/projects/handbook/#ip).
